title.zh: 卷二 本紀第二 武帝中
title.raw: 卷二 本紀第二 武帝中 Volume 2 Annals 2: Emperor Wu 2

sentences.zh: 七年正月己未，振旅于京師。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year, on the day jiwei, he led the army back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year (411), on the day jiwei, Gaozu marched his troops back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 改授大將軍、揚州牧，給班劍二十人，本官悉如故，固辭。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as Grand General and Governor of Yangzhou, granted twenty ceremonial swords, and all his original offices were left unchanged; he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: The court offered him Grand General and Governor of Yangzhou, with twenty ceremonial swords and all his old posts unchanged. He refused.

sentences.zh: 凡南北征伐戰亡者，並列上賻贈。

translations.literal: All who had died in battle on the northern and southern campaigns were to be listed and presented for funeral subsidies.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a full list of those killed in the northern and southern campaigns, with funeral grants for each.

sentences.zh: 尸喪未反，遣主帥迎接，致還本土。

translations.literal: Where the dead had not yet been brought back, he sent the commanders to receive them and return them to their native districts.
translations.idiomatic: Where bodies had not yet come home, he sent the field commanders to escort them back to their home districts.

sentences.zh: 二月，盧循至番禺，為孫季高所破，收餘眾南走。

translations.literal: In the second month, Lu Xun reached Panyu, was defeated by Sun Jigao, gathered his remaining forces, and fled south.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Lu Xun reached Panyu. Sun Jigao defeated him; he gathered what was left of his army and fled south.

sentences.zh: 劉藩、孟懷玉斬徐道覆于始興。

translations.literal: Liu Fan and Meng Huaiyu beheaded Xu Daofu at Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: At Shixing, Liu Fan and Meng Huaiyu beheaded Xu Daofu.

sentences.zh: 晉自中興以來，治綱大弛，權門并兼，強弱相凌，百姓流離，不得保其產業。

translations.literal: Since the Jin restoration, the bonds of governance had greatly slackened; powerful houses annexed one another, the strong bullied the weak, and the common people were displaced and could not keep their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jin court moved south, government had grown lax. Great families swallowed their neighbors, the strong preyed on the weak, and ordinary people lost their homes and could not hold on to their land.

sentences.zh: 桓玄頗欲釐改，竟不能行。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan had wished somewhat to reform this, but in the end could not carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan had tried to set things right, but never managed to.

sentences.zh: 公既作輔，大示軌則，豪強肅然，遠近知禁。

translations.literal: Once Gaozu had become regent, he displayed great norms; the powerful were awed into order, and near and far learned what was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Once Gaozu took power as regent, he laid down clear rules. The mighty fell silent, and everyone, near and far, knew the law.

sentences.zh: 至是會稽餘姚虞亮復藏匿亡命千餘人。

translations.literal: At this time Yu Liang of Yuyao in Kuaiji again harbored more than a thousand fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yu Liang of Yuyao in Kuaiji was again sheltering over a thousand fugitives.

sentences.zh: 公誅亮，免會稽內史司馬休之。

translations.literal: Gaozu executed Liang and dismissed Sima Xiuzhi, Interior Minister of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu had Liang executed and removed Sima Xiuzhi as Interior Minister of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 天子又申前命，公固辭。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven again pressed the earlier appointment upon him, and Gaozu firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pressed the earlier honors on him again. Gaozu refused.

sentences.zh: 於是改授太尉、中書監，乃受命。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was reassigned as Grand Commandant and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, and then accepted the commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Grand Commandant and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, and this time he accepted.

sentences.zh: 奉送黃鉞，解冀州。

translations.literal: The court presented the yellow battle-axe, and he relinquished Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent him the yellow battle-axe; he gave up Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 交州刺史杜慧度斬盧循，傳首京師。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jiaozhou Du Huidu beheaded Lu Xun and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Du Huidu, Inspector of Jiaozhou, killed Lu Xun and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 先是諸州郡所遣秀才、孝廉，多非其人，公表天子，申明舊制，依舊策試。

translations.literal: Previously the Recommended Scholars and Filial and Incorrupt candidates sent up by the provinces and commanderies had often not been fit men; Gaozu memorialized the Son of Heaven, clarifying the old regulations and restoring the written examinations as before.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial nominees for office had often been unworthy. Gaozu petitioned the throne to restore the old examination system.

sentences.zh: 征西將軍、荊州刺史道規疾患求歸，八年四月，改授豫州刺史，以後將軍、豫州刺史劉毅代之。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jingzhou Daogui, ill, asked to return; in the fourth month of the eighth year he was reassigned as Inspector of Yuzhou, and Rear General and Inspector of Yuzhou Liu Yi replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Daogui, General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jingzhou, fell ill and asked to come home. In the fourth month of the eighth year (412) he was made Inspector of Yuzhou; Liu Yi, Rear General and Inspector of Yuzhou, took his place in Jing.

sentences.zh: 毅與公俱舉大義，興復晉室，自謂京城、廣陵，功業足以相抗。

translations.literal: Yi had raised the great cause together with Gaozu and restored the Jin house; he considered that his achievements at the capital and at Guangling were enough to rival Gaozu's.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had joined Gaozu in restoring the Jin dynasty and thought his deeds at the capital and at Guangling matched Gaozu's own.

sentences.zh: 雖權事推公，而心不服也。

translations.literal: Though in power he deferred to Gaozu, in his heart he was not content.
translations.idiomatic: He yielded to Gaozu in public, but in his heart he would not submit.

sentences.zh: 毅既有雄才大志，厚自矜許，朝士素望者多歸之。

translations.literal: Yi possessed great talent and high ambition and thought highly of himself; many courtiers of long-standing repute turned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was talented, ambitious, and vain. Many senior officials looked to him instead.

sentences.zh: 與尚書僕射謝混、丹陽尹郗僧施並深相結。

translations.literal: He was deeply allied with Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Xie Hun and Chief of Danyang Xi Sengshi.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to Xie Hun, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Xi Sengshi, Chief of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 及西鎮江陵，豫州舊府，多割以自隨，請僧施為南蠻校尉。

translations.literal: When he went west to Jiangling, the old offices of Yuzhou were largely carved up for his own use, and he requested that Sengshi be made Commander Who Pacifies the Southern Man.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held Jiangling in the west, he took over much of the old Yuzhou establishment and asked that Sengshi be made Commander Who Pacifies the Southern Man.

sentences.zh: 既知毅不能居下，終為異端，密圖之。

translations.literal: Knowing that Yi could not remain subordinate and would in the end become a rebel, he secretly laid plans against him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu saw that Yi would never stay below him and would turn rebel; he began to plot in secret.

sentences.zh: 毅至西，稱疾篤，表求從弟兗州刺史藩以為副貳，偽許焉。

translations.literal: When Yi reached the west he claimed grave illness and memorialized, asking that his younger cousin Fan, Inspector of Yanzhou, be made his deputy; this was falsely granted.
translations.idiomatic: Yi reached the west, claimed to be gravely ill, and asked that his cousin Fan, Inspector of Yanzhou, be made his deputy. Gaozu pretended to agree.

sentences.zh: 九月，藩入朝，公命收藩及謝混，並於獄賜死。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, when Fan entered court, Gaozu ordered Fan and Xie Hun seized and both were granted death in prison.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Fan came to court. Gaozu had him and Xie Hun arrested and executed in prison.

sentences.zh: 自表討毅。

translations.literal: He himself memorialized to campaign against Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized to take the field against Yi.

sentences.zh: 又假黃鉞，率諸軍西征。

translations.literal: He was also lent the yellow battle-axe and led the armies west on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the yellow battle-axe and marched west at the head of the armies.

sentences.zh: 以前鎮軍將軍司馬休之為平西將軍、荊州刺史，兗州刺史道憐鎮丹徒，豫州刺史諸葛長民監太尉留府事，加太尉司馬、丹陽尹劉穆之建威將軍，配以實力。

translations.literal: Former General Who Guards the Army Sima Xiuzhi was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jingzhou; Inspector of Yanzhou Daoling garrisoned Dantu; Inspector of Yuzhou Zhuge Changmin oversaw the Grand Commandant's headquarters; and Grand Commandant Marshal and Chief of Danyang Liu Muzhi was made General Who Establishes Might, each posted with real force.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiuzhi became General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jingzhou; Daoling held Dantu; Changmin ran the capital in Gaozu's absence; Muzhi was made General Who Establishes Might—all with real troops behind them.

sentences.zh: 壬午，發自京師。

translations.literal: On the day renwu he set out from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renwu he marched out from the capital.

sentences.zh: 遣參軍王鎮惡、龍驤將軍蒯恩前襲江陵。

translations.literal: He sent Staff Officer Wang Zhen'e and Dragon-Chariot General Kuai En ahead to strike Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wang Zhen'e and Kuai En ahead to take Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 十月，鎮惡剋江陵，毅及黨與皆伏誅。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Zhen'e took Jiangling; Yi and his partisans were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Zhen'e took Jiangling. Yi and his followers were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 十一月己卯，公至江陵，下書曰：

translations.literal: On the day jimao of the eleventh month, Gaozu reached Jiangling and issued a proclamation, saying:
translations.idiomatic: On the day jimao in the eleventh month Gaozu reached Jiangling and issued a proclamation:

sentences.zh: 夫去弊拯民，必存簡恕，捨網修綱，雖煩易理。

translations.literal: "To remove abuses and save the people, one must preserve simplicity and forbearance; to cast aside the net and repair the cords, though troublesome, is easy to justify in principle."
translations.idiomatic: "To cure abuses and help the people, government must stay simple and humane. Tightening the law after years of disorder is hard work, but it is the right course."

sentences.zh: 江、荊彫殘，刑政多闕，頃年事故，綏撫未週。

translations.literal: Jiang and Jing were wasted and maimed; penal administration had many gaps; in recent years, because of upheaval, pacification had not been thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang and Jing were devastated; justice was patchy; years of turmoil had left the region half-settled.

sentences.zh: 遂令百姓疲匱，歲月滋甚，財傷役困，慮不幸生。

translations.literal: Thus the common people grew exhausted and impoverished, month by month the harm deepened, wealth was injured and corvée labor distressed, and I feared misfortune might arise.
translations.idiomatic: The people grew poorer every month, taxes and labor broke them, and I feared worse would follow.

sentences.zh: 凋殘之餘，而不減舊，刻剝徵求，不循政道。

translations.literal: On what remained of the wasted land, levies were not reduced from old levels; exactions and requisitions did not follow the way of government.
translations.idiomatic: Even on ruined ground the old levies stood. Officials squeezed the people without regard to law.

sentences.zh: 宰莅之司，或非良榦，未能菲躬儉，[1]苟求盈給，積習生常，漸不知改。

translations.literal: The officials who presided over districts were not always capable men; they could not restrain themselves in frugality, [1] but sought only to fill quotas; accumulated habit became custom, and gradually they no longer knew how to change.
translations.idiomatic: Many local magistrates were unfit. They would not live plainly [1] but chased every quota until waste became habit and reform seemed impossible.

sentences.zh: 近因戎役，來涉二州，踐境親民，愈見其瘼，思欲振其所急，卹其所苦。

translations.literal: Recently, because of the military campaign, I have come to these two provinces; treading the borders and facing the people, I have seen their afflictions all the more clearly, and I wish to rouse what is urgent and relieve what is bitter.
translations.idiomatic: This campaign has brought me into both provinces. Seeing the people myself, I know their distress and mean to ease what hurts them most.

sentences.zh: 凡租稅調役，悉宜以見戶為正。

translations.literal: All rent, tax, and corvée levies should be based entirely on registered households as they stand.
translations.idiomatic: All rent, tax, and labor duties shall be assessed only on actual registered households.

sentences.zh: 州郡縣屯田池塞，諸非軍國所資，利入守宰者，今一切除之。

translations.literal: Garrison fields, ponds, and passes in the provinces, commanderies, and counties—whatever did not serve military or state needs but whose profits went to the guarding magistrates—are now all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial garrison farms, ponds, and toll stations that served private profit rather than the army or the state are abolished at once.

sentences.zh: 州郡縣吏，皆依尚書定制實戶置。

translations.literal: Officials in the provinces, commanderies, and counties shall all be appointed according to the Masters of Writing's fixed quotas for actual households.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial, commandery, and county staffs shall be set only at the numbers the Masters of Writing allow for real households.

sentences.zh: 臺調癸卯梓材，庚子皮毛，可悉停省，別量所出。

translations.literal: The court requisitions of guimao timber and gengzi hides may all be halted and reduced; other sources shall be measured instead.
translations.idiomatic: Court demands for guimao timber and gengzi hides are suspended; other supplies will be found.

sentences.zh: 巴陵均折度支，依舊兵運。

translations.literal: The Ba-ling equalization and expenditure office shall follow the old military transport rules.
translations.idiomatic: The Ba-ling equalization office shall return to the old military transport system.

sentences.zh: 原五歲刑已下。

translations.literal: Pardon all punishments of five years or less.
translations.idiomatic: All sentences of five years or less are pardoned.

sentences.zh: 凡所質錄賊家餘口，亦悉原放。

translations.literal: All dependents of rebel households held as pledges are likewise to be released.
translations.idiomatic: Dependents taken hostage from rebel families are also freed.

sentences.zh: 以荊州十郡為湘州，公乃進督。

translations.literal: Ten commanderies of Jingzhou were made into Xiangzhou, and Gaozu then advanced as supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Ten commanderies of Jing were split off as Xiang province, and Gaozu took overall supervision.

sentences.zh: [2]以西陽太守朱齡石為益州刺史，率眾伐蜀。

translations.literal: [2] Administrator of Xiyang Zhu Lingshi was made Inspector of Yizhou and led the armies to attack Shu.
translations.idiomatic: [2] Zhu Lingshi, Administrator of Xiyang, was made Inspector of Yizhou and marched against Shu.

sentences.zh: 進公太傅、揚州牧，加羽葆鼓吹，班劍二十人。

translations.literal: Gaozu was promoted to Grand Tutor and Governor of Yangzhou, with feathered canopy, drums, and whistles, and twenty ceremonial swords.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was made Grand Tutor and Governor of Yangzhou, with imperial music and twenty ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 九年二月乙丑，公至自江陵。

translations.literal: On the day yichou of the second month of the ninth year, Gaozu returned from Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yichou in the second month of the ninth year (413) Gaozu returned from Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 初諸葛長民貪淫驕橫，為士民所患苦，公以其同大義，優容之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhuge Changmin had been greedy, licentious, arrogant, and overbearing, a affliction to scholars and commoners; Gaozu, because he had shared the great cause, treated him with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Changmin had long been greedy, brutal, and hated by the people. Gaozu had tolerated him because they had fought together for the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 劉毅既誅，長民謂所親曰：「昔年醢彭越，今年誅韓信，禍其至矣。

translations.literal: After Liu Yi was executed, Changmin said to those close to him: "Last year they minced Peng Yue; this year they kill Han Xin—disaster is upon me.
translations.idiomatic: After Yi died, Changmin told his intimates, "Last year Peng Yue was boiled; this year Han Xin is killed. My turn is coming.

sentences.zh: 」將謀作亂。

translations.literal: " He was about to plot rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: " He began to plot rebellion.

sentences.zh: 公克期至京邑，而每淹留不進。

translations.literal: Gaozu had set a date to reach the capital, yet each day he delayed and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu had named a day to reach the capital, but lingered on the road.

sentences.zh: 公卿以下頻日奉候於新亭，長民亦驟出。

translations.literal: From the Three Dukes down, for days on end they went to wait upon him at Xinting; Changmin too came out repeatedly in haste.
translations.idiomatic: For days the highest officials waited on him at Xinting. Changmin kept hurrying out to meet him.

sentences.zh: 既而公輕舟密至，已還東府矣。

translations.literal: Presently Gaozu came secretly in a light boat and was already back at the eastern headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Then Gaozu slipped in by light boat and was already back at his eastern headquarters.

sentences.zh: 長民到門。

translations.literal: Changmin came to the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Changmin came to the gate.

sentences.zh: 引前，卻人閑語，凡平生於長民所不盡者，皆與及之。

translations.literal: Gaozu drew him forward, dismissed the attendants, and in private conversation went over everything in their lives that he had never yet said to Changmin.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu brought him in, sent everyone else away, and spoke with him at length about everything he had never yet said between them.

sentences.zh: 長民甚說。

translations.literal: Changmin was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Changmin was delighted.

sentences.zh: 已密命左右壯士丁旿等自幔後出，於坐拉焉。

translations.literal: He had already secretly ordered the strong men at his side, Ding Wu and the rest, to come out from behind the curtain and seize him where he sat.
translations.idiomatic: He had already told his strongmen, Ding Wu and the rest, to slip out from behind the curtain and seize him in his seat.

sentences.zh: 長民墜牀，又於地毆之，死於牀側。

translations.literal: Changmin fell from the couch; they beat him again on the ground, and he died beside the couch.
translations.idiomatic: Changmin fell from the couch. They beat him on the floor until he died beside it.

sentences.zh: 輿尸付廷尉。

translations.literal: His body was placed in a cart and handed over to the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: The body was carted to the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 并誅其弟黎民。

translations.literal: His younger brother Limin was also executed.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Limin was executed as well.

sentences.zh: 旿驍勇有氣力，時人為之語曰：「勿跋扈，付丁旿。」

translations.literal: Wu was fierce and brave and full of strength; at the time people made a saying of it: "Do not act the bully—hand it to Ding Wu."
translations.idiomatic: Wu was famously fierce. People said, "Don't play the tyrant—leave it to Ding Wu."

sentences.zh: 先是山湖川澤，皆為豪強所專，小民薪採漁釣，皆責稅直，至是禁斷之。

translations.literal: Previously, mountains, lakes, rivers, and marshes had all been monopolized by the powerful; common people gathering firewood, fishing, or cutting reeds all paid a tax; now this was forbidden and cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful families had seized lakes, rivers, and hills; even firewood and fishing carried a fee. That was now forbidden.

sentences.zh: 時民居未一，公表曰：

translations.literal: At the time the people were not yet settled in one place; Gaozu memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The people were still unsettled. Gaozu submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞先王制治，九土攸序，分境畫疆，各安其居。

translations.literal: I have heard that the former kings in establishing order arranged the nine domains in sequence, divided borders and drew boundaries, and each kept to his dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient kings ordered the realm by fixing borders so that each people could dwell in peace.

sentences.zh: 在昔盛世，人無遷業，故井田之制，三代以隆。

translations.literal: In past ages of flourishing rule, men did not change their occupations; thus the well-field system flourished through the Three Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: In great ages no one left his trade; that is why the well-field system lasted through the Three Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 秦革斯政，漢遂不改，富強兼并，於是為弊。

translations.literal: Qin overturned this policy; Han did not change it, and the strong annexed the rich—thus the abuse arose.
translations.idiomatic: Qin abolished that order; Han kept the change, and the strong swallowed the weak.

sentences.zh: 然九服弗擾，所託成舊，在漢西京，大遷田、景之族，以實關中，即以三輔為鄉閭，不復係之於齊、楚。

translations.literal: Yet the nine domains were not disturbed; what they relied on remained the old. In the Western Han capital, the clans of Tian and Jing were moved on a great scale to fill Guanzhong, and the Three Metropolises became their native hamlets, no longer tied to Qi and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Still the realm held together because people kept their roots. In Western Han the Tian and Jing clans were moved en masse into Guanzhong; the capital districts became home and they were cut off from Qi and Chu.

sentences.zh: 自永嘉播越，爰託淮、海，朝有匡復之算，民懷思本之心，經略之圖，日不暇給。

translations.literal: From the Yongjia turmoil onward, the court entrusted itself to the Huai and the sea; the court had plans to restore the realm, and the people cherished the wish to return to their roots; schemes of strategy left no day free.
translations.idiomatic: After Yongjia the court fled to the Huai and the sea. All wanted restoration, and the people longed for home, but war left no day for civil rule.

sentences.zh: 是以寧民綏治，猶有未遑。

translations.literal: Thus in settling the people and pacifying rule, there was still no leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Peaceful settlement had to wait.

sentences.zh: 及至大司馬桓溫，以民無定本，傷治為深，庚戌土斷，以一其業。

translations.literal: When Grand Marshal Huan Wen saw that the people had no fixed base and that harm to governance lay deep therein, in the year gengxu he carried out the land register to unify their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Marshal Huan Wen saw that people had no fixed domicile and government suffered for it, he carried out the gengxu land register in 365 to give everyone a single legal home.

sentences.zh: 于時財阜國豐，實由於此。

translations.literal: At that time wealth flourished and the state was rich—this was truly owing to that measure.
translations.idiomatic: The treasury grew rich because of it.

sentences.zh: 自茲迄今，彌歷年載，畫一之制，漸用頹弛。

translations.literal: From then until now, many years have passed; the unified system has gradually fallen into decay.
translations.idiomatic: Since then the unified system had slowly collapsed.

sentences.zh: 雜居流寓，閭伍弗修，王化所以未純，民瘼所以猶在。

translations.literal: Mixed residence and floating registration, neighborhood registers not kept in order—the royal transformation was therefore not pure, and the people's afflictions therefore remained.
translations.idiomatic: Migrants and false registers broke the wards; government never fully took hold, and the people's misery remained.

sentences.zh: 臣荷重任，恥責實深，自非改調解張，無以濟治。

translations.literal: I bear a heavy commission and am deeply ashamed of the gap between charge and result; unless I change the registers and loosen the bonds, I cannot bring order.
translations.idiomatic: I hold great power and am ashamed that rule still fails. Without fixing the registers I cannot govern.

sentences.zh: 夫人情滯常，難與慮始，所謂父母之邦以為桑梓者，誠以生焉終焉，敬愛所託耳。

translations.literal: Human feeling clings to the constant and finds it hard to plan at the beginning; what is called taking one's native district as one's mulberry tree is truly because one is born and dies there and the object of reverent love is entrusted there.
translations.idiomatic: People cling to habit and hate sudden change. They call their home a mulberry tree because they are born and buried there and their loyalty belongs there.

sentences.zh: 今所居累世，墳壟成行，敬恭之誠，豈不與事而至。

translations.literal: Where they now dwell for generations, graves and mounds stand in rows; the sincerity of reverence—how could it fail to attend upon the matter when it comes?
translations.idiomatic: Families have lived in one place for generations; their graves line the fields. How could they not care when the state asks them to move?

sentences.zh: 請準庚戌土斷之科，庶子本所弘，稍與事著。

translations.literal: I ask that the gengxu land-register statute be applied, so that the intent to honor native roots may be broadly carried out and may gradually show in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the gengxu land register be enforced again, so respect for native roots may guide policy.

sentences.zh: 然後率之以仁義，鼓之以威武，超大江而跨黃河，撫九州而復舊土，則戀本之志，乃速申於當年，[3]在始暫勤，要終所以能易。

translations.literal: Then, leading them with benevolence and righteousness and rousing them with martial might, crossing the great river and spanning the Yellow River, comforting the nine provinces and recovering the old lands—then the wish to cherish one's roots would quickly be fulfilled in that year, [3] a brief hardship at the start, but in the end the change could be made easy.
translations.idiomatic: Then, with benevolence and force together, we may cross the Yangtze and Yellow River, recover the north, and give every man his home again. [3] The pain at first will be brief; in the end the change will be easy.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下，垂矜萬民，憐其所失，永懷鴻雁之詩，思隆中興之業。

translations.literal: Bow your head, Your Majesty, pitying the myriad people, cherishing what they have lost, ever keeping in mind the ode of the wild geese, thinking to exalt the enterprise of restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty pities the people, remembers what they have lost, and keeps the ode of the wild geese in mind, longing to restore the realm.

sentences.zh: 既委臣以國重，期臣以寧濟，若所啟合允，請付外施行。

translations.literal: Having entrusted me with the weight of the state and expecting me to bring peace, if what I propose is fitting, I ask that it be sent out and put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: You have charged me with the realm and expect peace from me. If this plan is sound, let it be carried out.

sentences.zh: 於是依界土斷，唯徐、兗、青三州居晉陵者，不在斷例。

translations.literal: Thereupon land was registered according to boundaries; only those in Jinling from Xu, Yan, and Qing provinces were outside the statute.
translations.idiomatic: Land was then registered by district. Only households of Xu, Yan, and Qing living in Jinling were exempt.

sentences.zh: 諸流寓郡縣，多被併省。

translations.literal: Many of the floating commanderies and counties were merged or abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Many refugee commanderies and counties were merged or abolished.

sentences.zh: 以公領鎮西將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He was made General Who Guards the West and Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was made General Who Guards the West and Inspector of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 公固讓太傅、州牧及班劍，奉還黃鉞。

translations.literal: Gaozu firmly declined Grand Tutor, Governor of the province, and the ceremonial swords, and returned the yellow battle-axe.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu refused the Grand Tutorship, the governorship, and the ceremonial swords, and sent back the yellow battle-axe.

sentences.zh: 七月，朱齡石平蜀，斬偽蜀王譙縱，傳首京師。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Zhu Lingshi pacified Shu, beheaded the false King of Shu Qiao Zong, and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Zhu Lingshi conquered Shu, killed the pretender Qiao Zong, and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 九月，封公次子義真為桂陽縣公，以賞平齊及定盧循也。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Gaozu's second son Yizhen was enfeoffed as Duke of Guiyang, to reward the pacification of Qi and the defeat of Lu Xun.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Gaozu's second son Yizhen was made Duke of Guiyang, rewarding the conquest of Qi and the defeat of Lu Xun.

sentences.zh: 天子重申前命，授公太傅、揚州牧，加羽葆、鼓吹、班劍二十人。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven again pressed the earlier appointment: Gaozu was made Grand Tutor and Governor of Yangzhou, with feathered canopy, drums, whistles, and twenty ceremonial swords.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again pressed the old honors on him: Grand Tutor, Governor of Yangzhou, imperial music, and twenty ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 將吏百餘敦勸，乃受羽葆、鼓吹、班劍，餘固辭。

translations.literal: More than a hundred officers urged him earnestly; only then did he accept the feathered canopy, drums, whistles, and ceremonial swords; the rest he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Over a hundred officers begged him to accept. He took the music and swords but refused the rest.

sentences.zh: 十年，息民簡役。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he gave the people rest and simplified corvée.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (414) he eased burdens on the people and cut labor duties.

sentences.zh: 築東府，起府舍。

translations.literal: He built the eastern headquarters and raised the official residences.
translations.idiomatic: He built the eastern headquarters and its offices.

sentences.zh: 平西將軍、荊州刺史司馬休之，宗室之重，又得江漢人心，公疑其有異志，而休之兄子譙王文思在京師，招集輕俠，公執文思送還休之，令自為其所。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jingzhou Sima Xiuzhi was a man of weight in the imperial clan and had won the hearts of the Jiang and Han regions; Gaozu suspected he harbored a different intent. Xiuzhi's elder brother's son, the Marquis of Qiao Wen Si, was in the capital gathering daredevils; Gaozu seized Wen Si and sent him back to Xiuzhi, telling him to deal with the matter himself.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiuzhi, General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jingzhou, was a prince of the blood with a following in Jiang and Han. Gaozu distrusted him. Xiuzhi's nephew Wen Si was in the capital gathering ruffians; Gaozu arrested Wen Si and sent him to Xiuzhi to punish as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 休之表廢文思，并與公書陳謝。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi memorialized to dismiss Wen Si and also wrote Gaozu a letter of apology.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi memorialized to disown Wen Si and wrote Gaozu to apologize.

sentences.zh: 十一年正月，公收休之子文寶、兄子文祖，並於獄賜死，率眾軍西討。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eleventh year, Gaozu seized Xiuzhi's son Wenbao and his brother's son Wenzu and granted them death in prison, then led the armies west on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eleventh year (415) Gaozu had Wenbao and Wenzu executed in prison and marched west.

sentences.zh: 復加黃鉞，[4]領荊州刺史。

translations.literal: He was again given the yellow battle-axe [4] and took charge as Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was again given the yellow battle-axe [4] and made Inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，發京師，以中軍將軍道憐監留府事。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi he set out from the capital; Central Army General Daoling oversaw the headquarters left behind.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinsi he left the capital. Daoling ran affairs at headquarters.

sentences.zh: 休之上表自陳曰：

translations.literal: Xiuzhi memorialized in his own person, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi submitted a personal memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞運不常一，治亂代有，陽九既謝，圮終則泰。

translations.literal: I have heard that fortune is not constant, order and disorder succeed each other in turn; when the yang ninth calamity has passed, collapse at the end gives way to peace.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune never stays the same; order and chaos take turns. When the worst is past, ruin gives way to renewal.

sentences.zh: 昔篡臣肆逆，皇綱絕紐，卜世未改，[5]鼎祚再隆。

translations.literal: In former days the usurping minister ran riot, the imperial cords were severed, the allotted age was not yet changed, [5] and the sacred vessel was raised a second time.
translations.idiomatic: Once a usurper seized power and the dynasty seemed dead, yet the throne was restored [5] and the mandate lived again.

sentences.zh: 太尉臣裕威武明斷，道建義旗，除蕩元凶，皇居反正。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Liu Yu was martially awesome and brilliantly decisive; he raised the banner of righteousness, swept away the chief villain, and restored the imperial palace to right order.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Liu Yu was fierce and clear-sighted. He raised the righteous standard, destroyed the usurper, and brought the throne back to order.

sentences.zh: 布衣匹夫，匡復社稷，南剿盧循，北定廣固，千載以來，功無與等。

translations.literal: A commoner in plain cloth restored the altars of state; south he crushed Lu Xun, north he pacified Guanggu; for a thousand years there has been no achievement to match his.
translations.idiomatic: A man of no rank restored the dynasty; in the south he destroyed Lu Xun, in the north he took Guanggu. In a thousand years no one had done more.

sentences.zh: 由是四海歸美，朝野推崇。

translations.literal: From this the four seas turned their praise to him, and court and countryside alike held him up.
translations.idiomatic: All the realm praised him; court and countryside alike looked up to him.

sentences.zh: 既位窮台牧，權傾人主，不能以道處功，恃寵驕溢。

translations.literal: Once he had reached the summit as regional governor, his power tilted past that of the sovereign; he could not treat his achievements by the Way, but relied on favor and overflowed with arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: Once he stood at the peak of power as a regional lord, he overshadowed the throne. He would not govern his success with restraint and, swollen with favor, grew insolent.

sentences.zh: 自以酬賞既極，便情在無上，刑戮逆濫，政用暴苛。

translations.literal: He considered that rewards had already reached their limit, and his heart set itself on being above all; punishments and executions ran contrary and excessive, and governance relied on violence and severity.
translations.idiomatic: He thought he had been rewarded to the full and his heart aimed at being above everyone. He killed at whim; his rule was cruel and harsh.

sentences.zh: 問鼎之迹日彰，人臣之禮頓缺。

translations.literal: The traces of moving the sacred ding grew daily clearer; the rites owed by a minister were suddenly lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Day by day his ambition to seize the throne showed more clearly, and the duties of a subject were cast aside.

sentences.zh: 陛下四時膳御，觸事縣空，宮省供奉，十不一在。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's seasonal meals and daily fare—whenever one touched on something, the larder was empty; what the palace offices should supply was not one part in ten present.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's meals through the seasons—every need went unmet. The palace could supply scarcely one thing in ten.

sentences.zh: 皇后寢疾之際，湯藥不周，手與家書，多所求告。

translations.literal: When the Empress lay ill, broths and medicines were not adequate; he wrote household letters by hand with many requests and pleas.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress was ill, medicine was not provided as it should be. He wrote personal letters full of demands.

sentences.zh: 皆是朝士共所聞見，莫不傷懷憤歎，口不敢言。

translations.literal: These are all what the court gentlemen have jointly heard and seen; none do not grieve in heart and sigh in anger, but dare not speak with the mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Every courtier has seen or heard these things. All grieve and rage in silence.

sentences.zh: 前揚州刺史元顯第五息法興，桓玄之釁，逃遠於外，王路既開，始得歸本。

translations.literal: Fa Xing, fifth son of the former Governor of Yangzhou Yuan Xian—during Huan Xuan's outbreak he fled far abroad; when the royal road was reopened, he was at last able to return to his origins.
translations.idiomatic: Fa Xing, fifth son of the former Governor of Yangzhou Yuan Xian, had fled abroad during Huan Xuan's rebellion. When the throne was restored, he returned home.

sentences.zh: 太傅之胤，絕而復興，凡在有懷，誰不感慶。

translations.literal: A descendant of the Grand Tutor, cut off and then revived—who among all who have feeling would not be moved to rejoice?
translations.idiomatic: A line of the Grand Tutor's house, cut off and restored—who would not rejoice?

sentences.zh: 裕吞噬之心，不避輕重，以法興聰敏明慧，必為民望所歸，芳蘭既茂，內懷憎惡，乃妄扇異言，無罪即戮。

translations.literal: Yu's heart of devouring did not avoid light or heavy; because Fa Xing was clever and bright and would surely become what the people's hopes gathered to, the fragrant orchid already flourishing—within he harbored hatred, then falsely stirred up alien words and without guilt executed him at once.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's hunger for power knew no bounds. Fa Xing was clever and bright and would win the people's regard. Yu hated this flourishing talent, spread false charges, and put him to death though he was innocent.

sentences.zh: 大司馬臣德文及王妃公主，情計切逼，並狼狽請命。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal De Wen and the princesses of the king and imperial consorts, in heartfelt calculation pressed hard—altogether in desperate plight they begged for their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal De Wen and the royal princesses were driven to desperation and pleaded for their lives.

sentences.zh: 逆肆禍毒，誓不矜許，寃酷之痛，感動行路。

translations.literal: In rebellious wantonness he unleashed poison and cruelty, swearing not to spare; the pain of wrongful cruelty moved those on the road.
translations.idiomatic: He cruelly refused mercy. The injustice of it moved even passersby.

sentences.zh: 自以地卑位重，荷恩崇大，乃以庶孽與德文嫡婚，致茲非偶，實由威逼。

translations.literal: Considering himself low in standing but heavy in position, bearing great favor and exalted grace, he then paired an illegitimate child in marriage with De Wen's legitimate heir—a mismatch brought about entirely by intimidation.
translations.idiomatic: Though his birth was mean, his rank was high and he owed great favor. He forced De Wen's legitimate line to marry a bastard daughter—an unfitting match made by intimidation.

sentences.zh: 故衞將軍劉毅、右將軍劉藩、前將軍諸葛長民、尚書僕射謝混、南蠻校尉郗僧施，或盛勳德胤，令望在身，皆社稷輔弼，協讚所寄，無罪無辜，一旦夷滅。

translations.literal: Thus Guard General Liu Yi, Right General Liu Fan, Forward General Zhuge Changmin, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Xie Hun, and Chief of the Southern Man Xi Sengshi—some with great merit and noble descent, commanding reputation in their persons, all pillars of the altars of state, entrusted with joint support—without guilt, without fault, were in one morning exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Guard General Liu Yi, Right General Liu Fan, Forward General Zhuge Changmin, Vice Director Xie Hun, and Chief of the Southern Man Xi Sengshi—men of great merit and standing, pillars of the state—all were destroyed in a single morning, though they were guilty of nothing.

sentences.zh: 猜忍之性，終古所希。

translations.literal: A nature of suspicion and cruelty—rare through the ages.
translations.idiomatic: Such suspicion and cruelty are rare in all history.

sentences.zh: 臣自惟門戶衰破，賴之獲存，皇家所重，終古難匹。

translations.literal: I myself reflect that my house's gates have declined and been broken; relying on him I have been preserved; what the royal house values in me is unmatched through the ages.
translations.idiomatic: My own house was ruined; I have survived only through his protection. The throne has never relied on anyone as it has on me.

sentences.zh: 是以公私歸馮，事盡祗順。

translations.literal: Therefore in public and private all turned to Feng, and matters were entirely respectful and obedient.
translations.idiomatic: In public and private I gave him my full loyalty and obedience.

sentences.zh: 再授荊州，輒苦陳告，自以才弱位隆，不宜久荷分陝，屢求解任，必不見聽。

translations.literal: Again I was granted Jingzhou and bitterly submitted memorials; considering my talent weak and my position lofty, I should not long bear the division between the two halves, repeatedly seeking release from office—yet he would certainly not listen.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzhou was given me again, I pleaded repeatedly to be relieved. I said my ability was slight and my rank too high to hold such a post long, and asked again and again to resign. He would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 前經攜侍老母，半家俱西，凡諸子姪，悉留京輦。

translations.literal: Earlier I took my aged mother in attendance; half the household went west together; all my sons and nephews were left in the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier I brought my aged mother west with me, leaving half my household in the capital with all my sons and nephews.

sentences.zh: 臣兄子譙王文思，雖年少常人，粗免咎悔，性好交遊，未知防遠，羣醜交構，為其風聲。

translations.literal: My elder brother's son, Prince of Qiao Wen Si, though young was an ordinary man, broadly free of blame and regret; his nature loved making friends, and he did not know how to guard against what is distant; the crowd of villains joined plots and made him their wind and sound.
translations.idiomatic: My brother's son Wen Si, Prince of Qiao, was young but otherwise unremarkable. He loved company and did not see danger coming. Villains plotted around him and used him for their ends.

sentences.zh: 裕遂翦戮人士，遠送文思。

translations.literal: Yu then cut down gentlemen and sent Wen Si far away.
translations.idiomatic: Yu then killed his associates and had Wen Si sent away.

sentences.zh: 臣順其此旨，表送章節，請廢文思，改襲大宗，遣息文寶送女東歸。

translations.literal: I followed this intent of his, memorialized and sent the formal documents, requested that Wen Si be deposed, changed to inherit the major line, and sent my son Wen Bao escorting a daughter east in return.
translations.idiomatic: I did as he wished: I petitioned to depose Wen Si, name another heir of the main line, and sent my son Wen Bao east with my daughter.

sentences.zh: 自謂推誠奉順，理不過此。

translations.literal: I considered that in pushing sincerity and offering obedience, reason could not go beyond this.
translations.idiomatic: I believed I had shown every possible loyalty.

sentences.zh: 豈意裕苞藏禍心，遂見討伐，加惡文思，構生罪釁。

translations.literal: Who would have thought that Yu harbored a treacherous heart and then came to attack and punish, adding malice toward Wen Si and fabricating grounds for guilt?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yu had hidden his malice all along. He attacked me and heaped new charges on Wen Si.

sentences.zh: 羣小之言，遠近噂𠴲，而臣純愚，闇信必謂不然。

translations.literal: The words of the petty crowd, near and far, buzzed with slander; yet I, purely foolish, in darkness trusted that it must not be so.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men spread slander far and wide. I was foolish enough to believe it could not be true.

sentences.zh: 尋臣府司馬張茂度狼狽東歸，南平太守檀範之復以此月三日委郡叛逆，尋有審問，東軍已上。

translations.literal: Soon my headquarters Marshal Zhang Maodu fled east in desperate plight; the Governor of Nanping Tan Fanzhi again on the third of this month surrendered his province in rebellion; soon there were inquiries, and the eastern army had already advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Then my marshal Zhang Maodu fled east in disarray. On the third of this month Tan Fanzhi, Governor of Nanping, rebelled and gave up his province. The eastern army was already on the march.

sentences.zh: 裕今此舉，非有怨憎，正以臣王室之幹，位居藩岳，時賢既盡，唯臣獨存，規以翦滅，成其篡殺。

translations.literal: Yu's present campaign is not from any grudge or hatred; it is simply because I am a pillar of the royal house, occupying the position of a frontier lord, the men of the age are already exhausted and only I remain—he plans to cut me down and accomplish his usurpation and slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: This campaign is not born of personal hatred. I am a pillar of the throne and a great frontier lord; the worthies of the age are gone and I alone remain. He means to destroy me and seize power.

sentences.zh: 鎮北將軍臣宗之、青州刺史臣敬宣，並是裕所深忌憚，欲以次除蕩，然後傾移天日，於事可易。

translations.literal: Pacifying-the-North General Zongzhi and Governor of Qingzhou Jingxuan are both what Yu deeply fears and dreads; he wishes to remove and sweep them away in order, and then overturn the sun and sky—then the affair will be easy.
translations.idiomatic: Pacifying-the-North General Zongzhi and Governor of Qingzhou Jingxuan are men he deeply fears. He means to eliminate them one by one, then overturn the throne itself.

sentences.zh: 今荊、雍義徒，不召而集，子來之眾，其會如林。

translations.literal: Now the righteous followers of Jing and Yong gather without being summoned; the masses that come like sons assemble as thick as a forest.
translations.idiomatic: Now the loyal men of Jing and Yong rally without a summons. They come like sons, thick as a forest.

sentences.zh: 豈臣無德所能綏致，蓋七廟之靈，理貫幽顯。

translations.literal: How could it be that I have no virtue and could bring this about? It is rather that the spirits of the seven temples—reason runs through the hidden and the manifest.
translations.idiomatic: This is not my virtue alone. The spirits of the ancestral temple move heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 輒授文思振武將軍、南郡太守，宗之子竟陵太守魯軌進號輔國將軍。

translations.literal: I have forthwith appointed Wen Si General Who Quells Martial Affairs and Governor of Nanjun; Zongzhi's son Gui, Governor of Jingling, is advanced to General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: I have made Wen Si General Who Quells Martial Affairs and Governor of Nanjun, and Zongzhi's son Gui, Governor of Jingling, General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 臣今與宗之親御大眾，出據江津，案甲抗威，隨宜應赴。

translations.literal: I now, with Zongzhi, personally lead the great host forth, take position at the river crossing, set armor and resist with might, and respond as occasion requires.
translations.idiomatic: I now lead the main army with Zongzhi to the river crossing, ready to meet whatever comes.

sentences.zh: 今絳旗所指，唯裕兄弟父子而已。

translations.literal: Now where the crimson banners point, it is only Yu and his brothers and sons.
translations.idiomatic: Our banners are aimed only at Yu and his brothers and sons.

sentences.zh: 須剋蕩寇逆，尋續馳聞。

translations.literal: When the bandits and rebels have been swept away, I will immediately continue to report in haste.
translations.idiomatic: Once the rebels are crushed I will report at once.

sentences.zh: 由臣輕弱，致裕凌橫，上慚俯愧，無以厝顏。

translations.literal: Because I am light and weak, I have brought Yu's overbearing conduct upon us; above I am ashamed, below I blush—there is no place to set my face.
translations.idiomatic: My own weakness has let Yu run rampant. I am ashamed before heaven and cannot face the world.

sentences.zh: 休之府錄事參軍韓延之，故吏也，有幹用才能。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi's headquarters Record-Gentleman Han Yanzhi was a former subordinate, capable and talented.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yanzhi, Record-Gentleman on Xiuzhi's staff, had been his man before and was capable and able.

sentences.zh: 公未至江陵，密使與之書曰：「文思事源，遠近所知，去秋遣康之送還司馬君者，[6]推至公之極也。

translations.literal: Before Gaozu reached Jiangling, he secretly sent him a letter saying: "The source of the Wen Si affair is known near and far; last autumn I sent Kangzhi to return him to the Marshal's lord—[6] that was pushing to the utmost of fairness.
translations.idiomatic: Before Gaozu reached Jiangling, he secretly wrote to him: "Everyone knows how the Wen Si affair began. Last autumn I sent Kangzhi to return him to your lord the Marshal [6]—that was the utmost fairness.

sentences.zh: 而了不遜愧，又無表疏。

translations.literal: Yet he was not at all deferential or ashamed, and again there was no memorial or report.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he showed no shame and sent no memorial.

sentences.zh: 文思經正不反，此是天地之不容。

translations.literal: Wen Si, having been upright and not turning back—this is what heaven and earth cannot tolerate.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Si stood firm and would not yield. Heaven and earth cannot abide that.

sentences.zh: 吾受命西討，止其父子而已。

translations.literal: I have received the mandate to campaign west and stop at his father and son alone.
translations.idiomatic: I march west on imperial orders, and my quarrel is only with father and son.

sentences.zh: 彼土僑舊，為所驅逼，一無所問。

translations.literal: The émigré old families of that land, driven and compelled by them, will not be questioned at all.
translations.idiomatic: The old émigré families there, forced to follow them, will not be punished.

sentences.zh: 往年郗僧施、謝邵、任集之等，交構積歲，專為劉毅謀主，所以至此。

translations.literal: In former years Xi Sengshi, Xie Shao, Ren Jizhi, and others plotted together for accumulated years, exclusively serving as Liu Yi's chief strategists—therefore it came to this.
translations.idiomatic: In past years Xi Sengshi, Xie Shao, Ren Jizhi, and others spent years plotting for Liu Yi. That is how matters came to this pass.

sentences.zh: 卿等諸人，一時逼迫，本無纖釁。

translations.literal: You gentlemen and the rest were at one time compelled and pressed; originally there was not the slightest fault.
translations.idiomatic: You were all forced into it. You had no real guilt.

sentences.zh: 吾處懷期物，自有由來。

translations.literal: My disposition cherishes men of promise—there has always been a reason for it.
translations.idiomatic: I have always valued men of promise. You know my mind.

sentences.zh: 今在近路，正是諸人歸身之日。

translations.literal: Now on the near road, this is exactly the day for you gentlemen to return your persons.
translations.idiomatic: Now that I am near, this is your day to come back to me.

sentences.zh: 若大軍登道，交鋒接刃，蘭艾吾誠不分。

translations.literal: If the great army mounts the road and blades cross in the clash, I truly do not distinguish orchid from mugwort.
translations.idiomatic: If the army marches and swords meet, I will not spare the innocent with the guilty.

sentences.zh: 故具示意，并示同懷諸人。

translations.literal: Therefore I set forth the meaning in full and also show it to the gentlemen of like mind.
translations.idiomatic: I set this out fully and send it to all who share your mind.

sentences.zh: 」延之報曰：

translations.literal: " Yanzhi replied:
translations.idiomatic: " Yanzhi replied:

sentences.zh: 承親率戎馬，遠履西畿，闔境士庶，莫不恇駭。

translations.literal: I have received that you personally lead armed horses and have come far, treading the western capital region; the gentry and common people of the whole territory—none are not terrified and dismayed.
translations.idiomatic: You lead your army far into the western capital. Every man in the region is terrified.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 莫知師出之名故也。

translations.literal: No one knows the name of the army's going forth.
translations.idiomatic: No one knows why the army has come.

sentences.zh: 今辱來疏，始知以譙王前事，良增歎息。

translations.literal: Now, insulted by your coming letter, I begin to know that it is on account of the Prince of Qiao's former affair—truly this increases sighing.
translations.idiomatic: Your letter tells me at last that this is about the Prince of Qiao. That only deepens my grief.

sentences.zh: 司馬平西體國忠貞，欵愛待物，當於古人中求耳。

translations.literal: Marshal of the Pacifying West—his body serves the state with loyalty and purity, treats men with sincere affection; one should seek him among the men of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: The Pacifying West Marshal serves the state with loyal devotion and treats men with open heart. Such a man belongs among the ancients.

sentences.zh: 以君公有匡復之勳，家國蒙賴，推德委誠，每事詢仰。

translations.literal: Because you, lord, have the achievement of restoration, the house and state rely on you; you push virtue and entrust sincerity—on every matter I look up in inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: You restored the dynasty and the realm depends on you. I have always trusted your virtue and sought your counsel on every matter.

sentences.zh: 譙王往以微事見劾，猶自表遜位；

translations.literal: The Prince of Qiao, on a slight matter, was impeached and still himself memorialized yielding his position;
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qiao was charged on a small matter and still offered to step down;

sentences.zh: 況以大過而當默然邪。

translations.literal: how much the more, faced with a great fault, should he have remained silent?
translations.idiomatic: how much less could he stay silent when charged with a grave fault?

sentences.zh: 但康之前言有所不盡，故重使胡道諮白所懷。

translations.literal: Only Kangzhi's earlier words did not exhaust the matter, so I again sent Hu Daozi to speak plainly what was in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzhi's message did not say everything, so I sent Hu Daozi to speak my mind plainly.

sentences.zh: 道未及反，已奏表廢之，所不盡者命耳。

translations.literal: The envoy had not yet returned when a memorial was already submitted deposing him—what was not exhausted was fate alone.
translations.idiomatic: Before the envoy returned, you had already petitioned to depose him. Fate, not friendship, finished the matter.

sentences.zh: 推寄相與之懷，正當如此？

translations.literal: Is this how the trust mutually entrusted between us should be?
translations.idiomatic: Is this how friends treat one another?

sentences.zh: 有何不可，便興兵戈。

translations.literal: What could not be accepted, that you should raise arms and weapons?
translations.idiomatic: What could not be settled except by war?

sentences.zh: 自義旗秉權以來，四方方伯，誰敢不先相諮疇，而逕表天子邪。

translations.literal: Since the righteous banner took power, which regional lord of the four directions has dared not first consult with you in turn, yet go straight to memorializing the Son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Since you took power, which frontier lord has dared report straight to the throne without consulting you first?

sentences.zh: 譙王為宰相所責，又表廢之，經正何歸，表使何因，可謂「欲加之罪，其無辭乎」！

translations.literal: The Prince of Qiao was reproved by the chief minister and again memorialized deposing him—where does the rectitude go, what cause does the memorial have? One may say, "When one wishes to impose guilt, there is no lack of words!"
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qiao was rebuked by the chief minister, and you petitioned again to depose him. Where is the justice, and what ground for the memorial? It is truly "when you wish to fix guilt, words are never lacking."

sentences.zh: 劉裕足下，海內之人，誰不見足下此心，而復欲欺誑國士！

translations.literal: Liu Yu, beneath your feet—all within the seas, who does not see this heart of yours, yet you still wish to deceive and beguile the men of the state!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu, everyone under heaven sees your heart. Yet you still try to deceive the realm!

sentences.zh: 天地所不容，在彼不在此矣。

translations.literal: What heaven and earth cannot tolerate lies with you, not with us.
translations.idiomatic: What heaven and earth cannot abide is on your side, not ours.

sentences.zh: 來示言「處懷期物，自有由來」。

translations.literal: Your letter says, "My disposition cherishes men of promise—there has always been a reason for it."
translations.idiomatic: You write, "I have always valued men of promise. You know my mind."

sentences.zh: 今伐人之君，啗人以利，真可謂「處懷期物，自有由來」者矣。

translations.literal: Now attacking another's lord and feeding men with profit—truly this may be called "cherishing men of promise—there has always been a reason for it."
translations.idiomatic: Now you attack a lord and bait men with profit. That is your "cherishing men of promise."

sentences.zh: 劉藩死於閶闔之內，諸葛斃於左右之手，甘言詫方伯，襲之以輕兵，遂使席上靡款懷之士，閫外無自信諸侯，以是為得算，良可恥也。

translations.literal: Liu Fan died within the Changle Gate; Zhuge perished at the hands of those beside him; sweet words deceived the regional lords, and light troops struck them—thus on the mats there were no gentlemen of sincere hearts, and beyond the gates no regional lords who trusted themselves; to take this as gaining one's reckoning is truly shameful.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fan died inside the Changle Gate; Zhuge died by assassins at his side. You flattered the lords with sweet words, then struck with light troops. No honest man sat at court; no lord beyond the gates trusted himself. To call that strategy is shameful.

sentences.zh: 貴府將佐及朝廷賢德，寄性命以過日，心企太平久矣。

translations.literal: The assistants of your headquarters and the worthy men of the court entrust their lives to passing the days; in heart they long for great peace—long indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Your staff and the court's worthies live from day to day, longing for peace.

sentences.zh: 吾誠鄙劣，嘗聞道於君子。

translations.literal: I am truly base and inferior; I have once heard the Way from gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: I am a humble man, but I have learned something from gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 以平西之至德，寧可無授命之臣乎！

translations.literal: With the Pacifying West's utmost virtue, could there be no minister who received the mandate?
translations.idiomatic: With such a lord as the Pacifying West, can he lack men who will die for him?

sentences.zh: 未能自投虎口，比迹郗、任之徒明矣。

translations.literal: That I could not throw myself into the tiger's mouth—compared with men like Xi and Ren, this is clear.
translations.idiomatic: I will not throw myself into the tiger's mouth like Xi and Ren. That much is clear.

sentences.zh: 假令天長喪亂，九流渾濁，當與臧洪遊於地下，不復多言。

translations.literal: Suppose heaven were long in chaos and the nine streams muddied—I would wander underground with Zang Hong and would not speak further.
translations.idiomatic: If the world falls into endless chaos, I will join Zang Hong in the grave. I have no more to say.

sentences.zh: 公視書歎息，以示諸佐曰：「事人當如此。」

translations.literal: Gaozu read the letter and sighed, showing it to his assistants and saying: "To serve a man should be like this."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu read the letter, sighed, and showed it to his staff. "To serve one's lord should be like this," he said.

sentences.zh: 三月，軍次江陵。

translations.literal: In the third month the army halted at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the army reached Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 初雍州刺史魯宗之常慮不為公所容，與休之相結，至是率其子竟陵太守軌會于江陵。

translations.literal: Earlier the Governor of Yongzhou Zongzhi had constantly feared he would not be tolerated by Gaozu; he allied with Xiuzhi, and at this time led his son Gui, Governor of Jingling, to join Xiuzhi at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zongzhi, Governor of Yongzhou, had feared Gaozu would not spare him. He joined Xiuzhi, and now came with his son Gui, Governor of Jingling, to meet him at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 江夏太守劉虔之邀之，軍敗見殺。

translations.literal: The Governor of Jiangxia Liu Qianzhi intercepted them; the army was defeated and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qianzhi, Governor of Jiangxia, intercepted them. Their force was beaten and Qianzhi was killed.

sentences.zh: 公命彭城內史徐逵之、參軍王允之出江夏口，復為軌所敗，並沒。

translations.literal: Gaozu ordered the Interior Minister of Pengcheng Xu Daozhi and Staff Officer Wang Yunzhi to go out from the Jiangxia crossing; they were again defeated by Gui and both perished.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent Xu Daozhi, Interior Minister of Pengcheng, and Wang Yunzhi, staff officer, out from the Jiangxia crossing. Gui defeated them and both were lost.

sentences.zh: 時公軍泊馬頭，即日率眾軍濟江，躬督諸將登岸，莫不奮踊爭先。

translations.literal: At that time Gaozu's army was moored at Matou; that same day he led the host of armies across the river, personally supervising the generals as they went ashore—none did not leap forward striving to be first.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's army lay at Matou. That day he crossed the river at the head of his forces and led the generals ashore. Every man strove to be first.

sentences.zh: 休之眾潰，與軌等奔襄陽，江陵平。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi's masses collapsed; with Gui and the rest he fled to Xiangyang, and Jiangling was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi's army broke. He fled with Gui and the rest to Xiangyang. Jiangling was taken.

sentences.zh: 加領南蠻校尉。

translations.literal: He was additionally made Chief of the Southern Man.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made Chief of the Southern Man.

sentences.zh: 將拜，值四廢日，佐史鄭鮮之、褚叔度、王弘、傅亮白遷日，不許。

translations.literal: When he was about to take office, it fell on a day of the four prohibitions; the clerks Zheng Xianzhi, Chu Shudu, Wang Hong, and Fu Liang asked to move the day—he did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When he was to take office, the day fell under the four prohibitions. His clerks Zheng Xianzhi, Chu Shudu, Wang Hong, and Fu Liang asked to postpone it. He refused.

sentences.zh: 下書曰：「此州積弊，事故相仍，民疲田蕪，杼軸空匱。

translations.literal: He issued a document saying: "This province has long accumulated abuses; incidents and troubles follow one another in succession; the people are weary, the fields overgrown, and the loom's shuttle-case is empty and exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: He issued an order: "This province has long been abused. Troubles follow troubles. The people are worn out, fields lie fallow, and households are empty.

sentences.zh: 加以舊章乖昧，事役頻苦，童耄奪養，老稚服戎，空戶從役，或越紼應召。

translations.literal: Added to this, old regulations are confused and obscure, corvée and service are frequent and bitter; children and the very old are robbed of their nurture, the aged and infants wear armor; empty households follow corvée, some crossing the mourning cord to answer summons.
translations.idiomatic: Old rules are tangled and service is crushing. Children and the aged are taken from their families; empty households are drafted, some called up even while in mourning.

sentences.zh: 每永懷民瘼，宵分忘寢，誠宜蠲除苛政，弘茲簡惠。

translations.literal: Whenever I long cherish the people's afflictions, I forget sleep at midnight; truly we should abolish harsh government and extend this simple kindness.
translations.idiomatic: When I think of the people's suffering I cannot sleep. Harsh rule must end and kindness must spread.

sentences.zh: 庶令凋風弊政，與事而新，寧一之化，成於朞月。

translations.literal: May the withering wind and abusive government, with the affairs, be made new; the transformation of tranquil unity be accomplished within a full month.
translations.idiomatic: May bad government pass away with these affairs and peace come within a month.

sentences.zh: 荊、雍二州，西局、蠻府吏及軍人年十二以還，六十以上，及扶養孤幼，單丁大艱，悉仰遣之。

translations.literal: In Jing and Yong, clerks of the western bureau and the barbarian headquarters, and soldiers twelve years and above, sixty and above, and those supporting orphans and the young, single men in great hardship—all are to be sent back relying on this.
translations.idiomatic: In Jing and Yong, clerks of the western offices and barbarian headquarters, soldiers twelve and under or sixty and over, and all who support orphans, the young, or face great hardship alone, are to be released.

sentences.zh: 窮獨不能存者，給其長賑。

translations.literal: Those poor and alone who cannot survive—give them long-term relief.
translations.idiomatic: Those too poor to live are to receive long-term relief.

sentences.zh: 府州久勤將吏，依勞銓序。

translations.literal: Officers and clerks of the headquarters and province who have long served in war are to be ranked in order according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and clerks who have long served in war are to be promoted according to merit.

sentences.zh: 并除今年租稅。」

translations.literal: And remit this year's land tax and levies."
translations.idiomatic: This year's taxes are remitted."

sentences.zh: 四月，公復率眾進討，至襄陽，休之奔羌。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Gaozu again led the host forward in campaign, reaching Xiangyang; Xiuzhi fled to the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Gaozu marched again, reached Xiangyang, and Xiuzhi fled to the Qiang.

sentences.zh: 天子復重申前命，授太傅、揚州牧，劍履上殿，入朝不趨，贊拜不名，加前部羽葆、鼓吹，置左右長史、司馬、從事中郎四人。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven again earnestly repeated the earlier commands, appointing him Grand Tutor and Governor of Yangzhou, sword and shoes in the hall, no hurrying in court entry, no naming in supportive obeisance, adding the forward feather-canopy and martial music, and setting four Left and Right Chiefs of Staff, Marshals, and Attending Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again pressed the earlier honors on him: Grand Tutor and Governor of Yangzhou, sword and shoes in the hall, no hurrying in court, no naming in obeisance, forward feather-canopy and martial music, and four chiefs of staff, marshals, and attending gentlemen on left and right.

sentences.zh: 封公第三子義隆為北彭城縣公。

translations.literal: Gaozu's third son Yilong was enfeoffed as Duke of North Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: His third son Yilong was made Duke of North Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 以中軍將軍道憐為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Central Army General Daoling was made Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Daoling, Central Army General, was made Governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 八月甲子，公至自江陵，奉還黃鉞，固辭太傅、州牧、前部羽葆、鼓吹，其餘受命。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi in the eighth month Gaozu arrived from Jiangling, returned the yellow battle-axe, firmly declined Grand Tutor, Governor, forward feather-canopy and martial music, and accepted the rest of the commands.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiazi in the eighth month Gaozu returned from Jiangling. He gave back the yellow battle-axe and refused Grand Tutor, Governor, and the forward canopy and music, but accepted the other honors.

sentences.zh: 朝議以公道尊勳重，不宜復施敬護軍，既加殊禮，奏事不復稱名。

translations.literal: Court discussion held that Gaozu's Way was honored and his merit heavy—it was not fitting to apply again the reverence due a Protector Army; since extraordinary rites had been added, in memorials his name was no longer spoken.
translations.idiomatic: The court held that Gaozu's rank and merit were too great for him to show the usual deference to the Protector Army. With these extraordinary honors, memorials no longer used his name.

sentences.zh: 以世子為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: The heir was made Governor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The heir was made Governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 十二年正月，詔公依舊辟士。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twelfth year an edict ordered Gaozu to recruit gentlemen as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twelfth year the emperor ordered Gaozu to recruit gentlemen as before.

sentences.zh: 加領平北將軍、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He was additionally made General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 增都督南秦，凡二十二州。

translations.literal: His supervision was increased to include Southern Qin—for a total of twenty-two provinces.
translations.idiomatic: His command was extended to Southern Qin, for twenty-two provinces in all.

sentences.zh: 公以平北文武寡少，不宜別置。

translations.literal: Gaozu considered that the civil and military staff of Pacifying the North were few and should not be set up separately.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu held that Pacifying the North had too few officials and soldiers to warrant a separate headquarters.

sentences.zh: 於是罷平北府，以併大府。

translations.literal: Thereupon he abolished the Pacifying-the-North headquarters and merged it into the great headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished the Pacifying-the-North office and merged it into his main headquarters.

sentences.zh: 以世子為豫州刺史。

translations.literal: The heir was made Governor of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The heir was made Governor of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 三月，加公中外大都督。

translations.literal: In the third month Gaozu was made Grand Commander of Court and Country.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he was made Grand Commander of Court and Country.

sentences.zh: 初公平齊，仍有定關、洛之意，值盧循侵逼，故其事不諧。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Gaozu had pacified Qi, he still had the intent to settle Guan and Luo; it happened that Lu Xun pressed in invasion, and therefore the affair did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying Qi he still meant to recover the Guan and Luo region, but Lu Xun's invasion forced him to set that plan aside.

sentences.zh: 荊、雍既平，方謀外略。

translations.literal: Once Jing and Yong were pacified, he then plotted outward expansion.
translations.idiomatic: With Jing and Yong secure, he turned to campaigns abroad.

sentences.zh: 會羌主姚興死，子泓立，兄弟相殺，關中擾亂，公乃戒嚴北討。

translations.literal: It happened that the Qiang ruler Yao Xing died; his son Hong established himself; brothers killed one another; Guanzhong was disturbed and chaotic—Gaozu then ordered martial readiness for a northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing of the Qiang died. His son Hong took the throne; brothers turned on one another and Guanzhong fell into chaos. Gaozu ordered the army to prepare for a northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 加領征西將軍、司豫二州刺史。

translations.literal: He was additionally made General Who Campaigns West and Governor of Si and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made General Who Campaigns West and Governor of Si and Yu.

sentences.zh: 以世子為徐、兗二州刺史。

translations.literal: The heir was made Governor of Xu and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The heir was made Governor of Xu and Yan.

sentences.zh: 下書曰：「吾倡大義，首自本州，克復皇祚，遂建勳烈，外夷勍敵，內清姦軌，皆邦人州黨竭誠盡力之效也。

translations.literal: He issued a document saying: "I raised the great cause, first from this province; I recovered the imperial fortune and then established meritorious achievement. Foreign barbarians as strong foes, within the realm clearing treacherous tracks—all are the effect of the men of our state and province exhausting sincerity and strength."
translations.idiomatic: He issued an order: "I raised the righteous cause in this province, restored the throne, and built our achievement. Defeating foreign enemies abroad and traitors at home—all this is the work of our countrymen who gave their all."

sentences.zh: 情若風霜，義貫金石。

translations.literal: Affection like frost and wind; righteousness penetrating metal and stone.
translations.idiomatic: Their loyalty was fierce as frost; their duty firm as metal and stone.

sentences.zh: 今當奉辭西斾，有事關、河，弱嗣叨蒙，復忝今授，情事纏綿，可謂深矣。

translations.literal: Now I am about to take leave of the western banners and have business in Guan and He; the weak heir undeservedly receives favor, again bearing the present appointment—affairs of feeling are tangled and involved; one may say it is deep indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Now I march west toward Guan and the Yellow River. My young heir has been given office again though he is unworthy. The ties of family weigh heavily on me.

sentences.zh: 頃軍國務殷，刑辟未息，眷言懷之，能不多歎。

translations.literal: Recently military and state affairs have been pressing; punishments and executions have not ceased. Whenever I turn my regard and cherish them in mind, how can I not sigh greatly?
translations.idiomatic: War and government have pressed hard upon us and executions have not ceased. When I think of this, how can I not sigh?

sentences.zh: 其犯罪繫五歲以還，可一原遣。

translations.literal: Those whose crimes have been imprisoned for five years and back may all at once be pardoned and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: All prisoners of five years or less are to be pardoned and released.

sentences.zh: 文武勞滿未蒙榮轉者，便隨班序報。」

translations.literal: Civil and military men whose labor is complete yet have not received honorable transfer—let them be reported according to roster order."
translations.idiomatic: Officers and clerks who have completed their service but not received promotion are to be reported in roster order."

sentences.zh: 公受中外都督及司州，並辭大司馬琅邪王禮敬，朝議從之。

translations.literal: Gaozu accepted Grand Commander of Court and Country and Si province, and together declined the ceremonial reverence due the Grand Marshal, Prince of Langye; court discussion followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu accepted the grand command and Si province, and also declined the ceremonial reverence owed the Grand Marshal, Prince of Langye. The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 公欲以義聲懷遠，奉琅邪王北伐。

translations.literal: Gaozu wished with righteous renown to win the distant and to lead the Prince of Langye on a northern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu wished to win the distant lands by righteous fame and to lead the Prince of Langye north in person.

sentences.zh: 五月，羌偽黃門侍郎尹沖率兄弟歸順。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the false Qiang Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Yin Chong led his brothers in submission.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Yin Chong, false Qiang Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, came over with his brothers.

sentences.zh: 又加公北雍州刺史，前部羽葆、鼓吹，增班劍為四十人。

translations.literal: Gaozu was again made Governor of Northern Yong, with forward feather-canopy and martial music; ceremonial swords were increased to forty men.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made Governor of Northern Yong, with forward canopy, martial music, and forty ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 解中書監。

translations.literal: He was relieved of Supervisor of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned as Supervisor of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 八月丁巳，率大眾發京師。

translations.literal: On the day dingsi in the eighth month he led the great host forth from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingsi in the eighth month he led the main army out of the capital.

sentences.zh: 以世子為中軍將軍，監太尉留府事。

translations.literal: The heir was made Central Army General and oversaw the headquarters affairs left with the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: The heir was made Central Army General and oversaw affairs at the Grand Commandant's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 尚書右僕射劉穆之為左僕射，領監軍、中軍二府軍司，入居東府，總攝內外。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Muzhi was made Left Vice Director, holding concurrently the army marshals of the Overseer Army and Central Army headquarters, entering and dwelling in the Eastern Headquarters, and taking overall charge of inner and outer affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Muzhi, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, became Left Vice Director and took charge of the Overseer Army and Central Army staffs at the Eastern Headquarters, directing affairs within and without.

sentences.zh: 九月，公次于彭城，加領徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Gaozu halted at Pengcheng and was additionally made Governor of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Gaozu halted at Pengcheng and was also made Governor of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是遣冠軍將軍檀道濟、龍驤將軍王鎮惡步向許、洛，羌緣道屯守，皆望風降服。

translations.literal: Earlier he had sent Champion General Tan Daoji and Flying-Dragon General Wang Zhen'e on foot toward Xu and Luo; along the road the Qiang garrisoned and guarded, all looking to the wind and submitting.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier he had sent Tan Daoji and Wang Zhen'e toward Xu and Lu. Qiang garrisons along the road surrendered as they advanced.

sentences.zh: 偽兗州刺史韋華先據倉垣，亦率眾歸順。

translations.literal: The false Governor of Yanzhou Wei Hua had first held Cangyuan and also led the masses in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Hua, the false Governor of Yanzhou, who held Cangyuan, also submitted with his forces.

sentences.zh: 公又遣北兗州刺史王仲德先以水軍入河。

translations.literal: Gaozu again sent Governor of Northern Yanzhou Wang Zhongde ahead with the water army to enter the river.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent Wang Zhongde, Governor of Northern Yanzhou, ahead with the fleet into the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 仲德破索虜於東郡涼城，進平滑臺。

translations.literal: Zhongde defeated the barbarians of the north at Liangcheng in Dongjun and advanced peacefully to Pingtai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde defeated the northern barbarians at Liangcheng in Dongjun and advanced to Pingtai without resistance.

sentences.zh: 十月，眾軍至洛陽，圍金墉。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the host of armies reached Luoyang and besieged Jinyong.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the army reached Luoyang and besieged Jinyong.

sentences.zh: 泓弟偽平南將軍洸請降，送于京師。

translations.literal: Hong's younger brother, the false Pacifying-the-South General Guang, requested surrender and was sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Guang, Hong's brother and false Pacifying-the-South General, surrendered and was sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 修復晉五陵，置守衞。

translations.literal: The five tombs of Jin were restored and guards were set.
translations.idiomatic: The five Jin imperial tombs were restored and guards were posted.

sentences.zh: 天子詔曰：

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven's edict said:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's edict said:

sentences.zh: 夫嵩、岱配極，則乾道增輝，藩嶽作屏，則帝王成務。

translations.literal: Song and Dai match the pole—then the way of Heaven adds its radiance; frontier mountains serve as screens—then emperors accomplish their task.
translations.idiomatic: When Song and Dai stand as the world's pillars, Heaven's way shines brighter; when frontier lords serve as the throne's screen, the emperor's work is done.

sentences.zh: 是以夏、殷資昆、彭之伯，有周倚齊、晉之輔。

translations.literal: Therefore Xia and Yin relied on the lords Kun and Peng; Zhou had Qi and Jin as its assistants.
translations.idiomatic: Xia and Yin relied on lords like Kun and Peng; Zhou leaned on Qi and Jin.

sentences.zh: 鑒諸前典，儀刑萬代，翼治扶危，靡不由此。

translations.literal: Reflecting on the former canon, taking them as models for ten thousand generations—supporting rule and propping up peril—none is not through this.
translations.idiomatic: The old canon shows that supporting the throne and saving the state in peril has always depended on such men.

sentences.zh: 太尉公命世天縱，齊聖廣淵，明燭四方，道光宇宙。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Liu Yu was by fate of the age Heaven-sent, equal to the sage, broad and deep; his clarity illumined the four directions, his Way's radiance filled the universe.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Liu Yu was Heaven's gift to the age—sagely, broad, and deep. His wisdom lit the four quarters; his virtue filled the world.

sentences.zh: 爰自□□初迪，則投懃王國，妖蝥孔熾，則功存社稷。

translations.literal: From the beginning when he first set forth on the road, he threw his diligence into service of the royal house; when the demon locusts were greatly blazing, his achievement preserved the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: From his first service to the throne, he gave himself wholly to the royal house. When rebellion raged, he preserved the altars of state [□].

sentences.zh: 固以四維是荷，萬邦攸賴者矣。

translations.literal: Thus he bore the four bonds on his shoulders; the ten thousand states relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: He bore the realm on his shoulders; all states relied on him.

sentences.zh: 暨桓玄僭逆，傾蕩四海，公深秉大節，靈武霆震，弘濟朕躬，再造王室。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan usurped and rebelled, overturning and shaking the four seas, Gaozu deeply held the great integrity; his spiritual martial thundered and quaked; he broadly succored Our person and remade the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan usurped power and shook the realm, Gaozu held fast to the highest duty. His martial spirit thundered forth; he saved the throne and remade the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 每惟勳德，銘于厥心，遂北清海、岱，南夷百越，荊、雍稽服，庸、岷順軌，剋黜方難，式遏寇虐。

translations.literal: Whenever I reflect on his merit and virtue, it is engraved in my heart. Then north he cleared the sea and Mount Tai, south he subdued the hundred Yue; Jing and Yong bowed in submission; Yong and Min followed the track; he overcame and removed regional difficulties and checked and halted bandit cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: His merit is engraved on my heart. He pacified the north to the sea and Mount Tai, subdued the south to the hundred Yue, brought Jing and Yong to heel, and checked every rebel and raider.

sentences.zh: 及阿衡王猷，班序內外，仰興絕風，傍嗣逸業。

translations.literal: And as he assisted in the royal plan, ordering inner and outer ranks, he raised up the dying wind and continued the lost enterprise beside it.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister he ordered the court within and without, revived dying customs, and continued the work of fallen sages.

sentences.zh: 秉禮以整俗，遵王以垂訓，聲教遠被，無思不洽。

translations.literal: Holding rites to regulate custom, following the king to hand down instruction—his sound teaching spread far; none whom he thought of was not brought to harmony.
translations.idiomatic: He governed by ritual, taught by the kingly way, and spread civilization until all were brought to harmony.

sentences.zh: 爰暨木居海處之酋，被髮彫題之長，莫不忘其陋險，九譯來庭，此蓋播諸徽策，靡究其詳者也。
