translations.literal: Down to the chiefs who dwelt in trees by the sea and the elders with disheveled hair and tattooed foreheads—none did not forget their rugged passes; through nine translations they came to court. This is broadly set forth in fine records; none can exhaust the detail.
translations.idiomatic: Even chiefs who lived in trees by the sea and elders with tattooed faces forgot their remote homelands and came to court through many interpreters. The records praise this, though no account can tell it all.

sentences.zh: 曩者永嘉不綱，諸夏幅裂，終古帝居，淪胥戎虜，永言園陵，率土同慕。

translations.literal: In former days the Yongjia reign lost its bonds; the many Xia were torn apart; the imperial dwelling of old was lost to barbarian captors; long speaking of the park tombs, all within the lands shared the same longing.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongjia the dynasty lost its hold; the realm was torn apart; the old capital fell to barbarians; every heart longed for the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 公明發遐慨，撫機電征，親董侯伯，稜威致討。

translations.literal: Gaozu with bright awakening and distant indignation grasped the moment like lightning in campaign; personally he oversaw the marquises and earls; his awl-edge authority brought punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu seized the moment with righteous wrath, led the lords in person, and struck with irresistible force.

sentences.zh: 旗旝首塗，則八表響震；

translations.literal: When the banners first took the road, the eight regions echoed and quaked;
translations.idiomatic: When his banners first moved, the eight regions trembled;

sentences.zh: 偏師先路，則多壘雲徹。

translations.literal: when the detached army went ahead on the road, the many ramparts were pierced like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: when his vanguard advanced, fortress after fortress fell.

sentences.zh: 舊都載清，五陵復禮，百城屈膝，千落影從。

translations.literal: The old capital was cleared and restored; the five tombs received rites again; a hundred cities bent the knee; a thousand settlements followed like shadows.
translations.idiomatic: The old capital was restored; the five tombs received rites again; cities bowed and villages followed.

sentences.zh: 自篇籍所載，生民以來，勳德懋功，未有若此之盛者也。

translations.literal: From what the books and records contain, since living men arose, in meritorious virtue and great achievement there has been none so grand as this.
translations.idiomatic: In all the records of history, no man alive has achieved merit such as this.

sentences.zh: 昔周、呂佐叡聖之主，因三分之形，把旄仗鉞，一時指麾，皆大啟疆宇，跨州兼國。

translations.literal: In former times Zhou and Lü assisted sage rulers of the age; taking advantage of the form of tripartite division, they grasped yak-tail banners and battle-axes; at one time they pointed and commanded—all greatly opened frontier territory and spanned provinces, holding several states.
translations.idiomatic: Of old the dukes of Zhou and Lü served sage rulers, held command across divided realms, and opened vast territories spanning many provinces.

sentences.zh: 其在桓、文，方茲尤儉，然亦顯被寵章，光錫殊品。

translations.literal: Even in the cases of Duke Huan and Duke Wen, compared with this they were especially sparing—yet they still clearly received favoring seals and were brightly granted extraordinary ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Even Duke Huan and Duke Wen of Qi received far less, yet they were richly honored with extraordinary rank.

sentences.zh: 況乃獨絕百代，顧邈前烈者哉！

translations.literal: How much the more for one who stands alone above a hundred generations and looks down on former blazing deeds!
translations.idiomatic: How much more should such a man as this be honored, who surpasses every age and every predecessor!

sentences.zh: 朕每弘鑒古訓，思遵令圖。

translations.literal: I each day broadly reflect on the ancient instructions and think of following the present chart.
translations.idiomatic: Each day I study the ancients and seek to follow their example.

sentences.zh: 以公深秉沖挹，用闕大禮，天人引領，于茲歷載。

translations.literal: Because Gaozu deeply holds modest restraint, the great rites are thereby lacking; Heaven and men stretch their necks—through these years it has accumulated.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu in his humility has declined the greatest honors, though Heaven and men have long awaited them.

sentences.zh: 況今禹迹齊軌，九隩同文，司勳抗策，普天增佇。

translations.literal: Moreover, now the traces of Yu are level on the wheel; the nine borderlands share the same script; the Director of Merit raises his memorial and all under Heaven increases their waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Now the empire is united, all lands share one script, and the Director of Merit urges that the realm's hope be answered.

sentences.zh: 遂公高挹，大愆國章，三靈眷屬，朕實祗懼。

translations.literal: Yet Gaozu holds himself high and restrains himself—a great fault against the state's regulations; the three spirits look to him with attachment—I am truly in reverent fear.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Gaozu still holds back, to the state's great loss. Heaven watches; I am filled with dread.

sentences.zh: 便宜顯答羣望，允崇盛典。

translations.literal: It is fitting that he clearly answer the hopes of the masses and allow the grand ceremony to be exalted.
translations.idiomatic: It is right that he accept the people's hope and permit this supreme honor.

sentences.zh: 其進位相國，總百揆，揚州牧，封十郡為宋公，備九錫之禮，加璽綬、遠遊冠，位在諸侯王上，加相國綠綟綬。

translations.literal: Let him advance in rank to Chief Minister, oversee the hundred duties, be Governor of Yangzhou, be enfeoffed with ten commanderies as Duke of Song, be provided the rites of the nine bestowals, add imperial seals and cord and the far-wandering cap; his rank is above the feudal princes and kings; add the Chief Minister's green sash and cord.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be made Chief Minister, oversee all government, remain Governor of Yangzhou, be enfeoffed as Duke of Song over ten commanderies, receive the Nine Bestowals, the imperial seals and cord, and the far-wandering cap, and rank above all princes and kings, with the Chief Minister's green sash.

sentences.zh: 策曰：

translations.literal: The mandate document says:
translations.idiomatic: The mandate reads:

sentences.zh: 朕以寡昧，仰贊洪基，夷羿乘釁，蕩覆王室，越在南鄙，遷于九江。

translations.literal: I, being dull and dim, look up to assist the great foundation; Yi of the east seized the opportunity; he overturned and capsized the royal house; he crossed to the southern marches and moved to Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: I am dull and weak, yet I uphold the great foundation. Yi seized his chance, overthrew the throne, fled south, and moved the court to Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 宗祀絕饗，人神無位，提挈羣凶，寄命江滸。

translations.literal: The ancestral sacrifices were cut off; men and spirits had no place; I was dragged along with the crowd of villains and entrusted my life to the riverbank.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral rites ceased; gods and men were displaced. I was dragged along with rebels and lived as a refugee on the river.

sentences.zh: 則我祖宗之業，奄墜于地，七百之祚，翦焉既傾，若涉淵海，罔知攸濟。

translations.literal: Then the enterprise of our ancestors suddenly fell to the ground; the fortune of seven hundred years was already cut down and toppled; as if crossing a deep sea, I knew not what to cross to.
translations.idiomatic: Our ancestors' legacy collapsed; seven hundred years of fortune fell. I was as one drowning in a deep sea, with no shore in sight.

sentences.zh: 天未絕晉，誕育英輔，振厥弛維，再造區宇，興亡繼絕，俾昏作明。

translations.literal: Heaven had not yet cut off Jin; it brought forth an heroic assistant; he shook the slackened cords and remade the realm within the four quarters; he continued the dying and restored the cut off, making the dim bright.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven did not yet end Jin. It sent a great helper who tightened the loosened bonds, remade the realm, restored the fallen, and brought light to the dark.

sentences.zh: 元勳至德，朕實賴焉。

translations.literal: In primordial merit and utmost virtue—I truly rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: In supreme merit and virtue I truly rely on him.

sentences.zh: 今將授公典策，其敬聽朕命：

translations.literal: Now I will confer on Gaozu the canonical mandate; respectfully hear my command:
translations.idiomatic: Now I confer the canonical mandate upon him. Hear my command:

sentences.zh: 乃者桓玄肆僭，滔天泯夏，拔本塞源，顛倒六位，庶僚俛眉，四方莫卹。

translations.literal: In former days Huan Xuan ran riot in usurpation, flooding Heaven and extinguishing Xia; he uprooted the root and blocked the source, overturning the six positions; the many officials bowed their brows; the four directions none consoled.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan usurped power, overwhelmed Heaven, and destroyed the dynasty. He uprooted the state and overturned the cosmic order. Officials bowed in fear; none could save the realm.

sentences.zh: 公精貫朝日，氣凌霄漢，奮其靈武，大殲羣慝，剋復皇邑，奉帝歆神。

translations.literal: Gaozu's essence penetrated the morning sun; his spirit towered the Milky Way; he roused his spiritual martial and greatly slaughtered the crowd of villains; he recovered the imperial city and presented the emperor to the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's spirit matched the sun; his valor reached the heavens. He crushed the rebels, recovered the capital, and restored the emperor to the throne.

sentences.zh: 此公之大節，[7]始於勤王者也。

translations.literal: This is Gaozu's great integrity, [7] beginning in service to the kingly cause.
translations.idiomatic: This was his first great act of loyalty [7], when he served the righteous cause.

sentences.zh: 授律羣后，泝流長騖，薄伐崢嶸，獻捷南郢，大憝折首，羣逆畢夷，三光旋采，舊物反正。

translations.literal: He received the law among the lords, went upstream in long gallop, made light campaign against the lofty peaks, presented victory at Southern Jing; the great villain broke his head; the crowd of rebels were all leveled; the three luminaries turned their light; old things returned to correctness.
translations.idiomatic: He took command among the lords, marched upstream, struck the highlands, and won victory at Southern Jing. The chief rebel was destroyed and all enemies swept away. The realm was restored to order.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too is Gaozu's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: This too was his achievement.

sentences.zh: 出藩入輔，弘茲保弼，阜財利用，繁殖生民，編戶歲滋，疆宇日啟，導德明刑，四境有截。

translations.literal: Going out to the frontier and entering as assistant, he enlarged this protection and support; he enriched goods and benefited use, bred and raised the living people; registered households yearly increased; the frontier realm daily opened; he guided virtue and clarified punishments—the four borders had boundaries.
translations.idiomatic: As minister at court and lord abroad, he enriched the people, increased households, extended the borders, governed by virtue, and brought peace to the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too is Gaozu's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: This too was his achievement.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑負眾，僭盜三齊，狼噬冀、青，虔劉沂、岱，介恃遐阻，仍為邊毒。

translations.literal: The Xianbei bore their masses and usurped and stole the three Qi; wolves devoured Ji and Qing; they reverently slaughtered Yi and Dai; relying on distant barriers, they again became border poison.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei seized the three Qi, ravaged Ji and Qing, slaughtered Yi and Dai, and from their distant strongholds plagued the borders.

sentences.zh: 公蒐乘秣駟，敻入遠疆，衝櫓四臨，萬雉俱潰，竊號之虜，顯戮司寇，拓土三千，申威龍漠。

translations.literal: Gaozu gathered chariots and fed the four horses, entered the far frontier; assault towers looked down on four sides; ten thousand ramparts all collapsed; the usurping-number barbarians were displayed in punishment before the Minister of Crime; he extended territory three thousand li and declared authority on the Dragon Desert.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu gathered his forces and drove deep into the frontier. His assault towers surrounded the enemy on every side; fortress after fortress fell. The usurpers were executed; three thousand li of territory were won and his authority proclaimed across the northern desert.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too is Gaozu's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: This too was his achievement.

sentences.zh: 盧循妖凶，伺隙五嶺，乘虛肆逆，侵覆江、豫，旍拂寰內，矢及王城，朝野喪沮，莫有固志，家獻徙卜之計，國議遷都之規。

translations.literal: Lu Xun, demonic and vicious, watched for a gap in the five ridges; riding the void he ran riot in rebellion, overthrowing and covering Jiang and Yu; his banners brushed the inner realm; his arrows reached the royal city; court and countryside lost heart; none had a firm will; families offered plans to move house; the state discussed plans to move the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun the rebel watched his chance in the south, swept through Jiang and Yu, and threatened the capital itself. Court and country lost heart; some urged moving the capital.

sentences.zh: 公乘轅南濟，義形于色，嶷然內湛，視嶮若夷，攄略運奇，英謨不世，狡寇窮衂，喪旗宵遁，俾我畿甸，拯於將墜。

translations.literal: Gaozu rode the shafts south across the river; righteousness showed in his face; within he was steep and deep; he regarded peril as level; he spread strategy and moved wonders; his heroic plan was not of the age; the cunning bandit was driven to extremity and lost his banners fleeing by night; he made our capital region be saved from about to fall.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu crossed the river in person, calm in the face of danger. By unmatched strategy he drove the rebel to flight by night and saved the capital from ruin.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too is Gaozu's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: This too was his achievement.

sentences.zh: 追奔逐北，揚旍江濆，偏旅浮海，指日遄至。

translations.literal: Pursuing the fleeing and chasing the north, he raised banners on the river's bank; a detached brigade floated on the sea and in a day arrived swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the fleeing enemy along the river and sent a fleet across the sea that arrived within days.

sentences.zh: 番禺之功，俘級萬數，左里之捷，魚潰鳥散。

translations.literal: At the achievement of Panyu the captives and severed heads were in the tens of thousands; at the victory of Zuoli the fish collapsed and birds scattered.
translations.idiomatic: At Panyu tens of thousands were captured; at Zuoli the enemy broke like fish and scattered like birds.

sentences.zh: 元凶遠迸，傳首萬里，海南肅清，荒服來款。

translations.literal: The chief villain fled far; his head was transmitted ten thousand li; Hainan was solemnly cleared; the wild domains came to offer friendship.
translations.idiomatic: The chief rebel fled far away; his head was sent a thousand leagues. The south was pacified and the frontier submitted.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too is Gaozu's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: This too was his achievement.

sentences.zh: 劉毅叛換，負釁西夏，凌上罔主，志肆姦暴，附麗協黨，扇蕩王畿。

translations.literal: Liu Yi changed in rebellion, bearing guilt in the western Xia; he insulted above and deceived the sovereign; his will ran riot in treacherous violence; he attached and clung to factions; he fanned and shook the royal capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi rebelled in the west, insulted the throne, and with his faction shook the capital.

sentences.zh: 公御軌以刑，消之不日，倉兕電泝，神兵風掃，罪人斯得，荊、衡清晏。

translations.literal: Gaozu controlled the track with punishment; within not a day he extinguished them; the storehouse rhinoceros went like lightning upstream; divine soldiers swept like wind; the guilty man was thereby obtained; Jing and Heng were clear and tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu struck with the law and destroyed them within a day. His army moved like lightning; the rebel was taken and Jing and Heng were pacified.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too is Gaozu's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: This too was his achievement.

sentences.zh: 譙縱怙亂，寇竊一隅，王化阻閡，三巴淪溺。

translations.literal: Qiao Zong relied on disorder; he bandited and stole one corner; royal transformation was blocked and barred; the three Ba were drowned and submerged.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zong seized a corner of the realm, blocked royal authority, and drowned the three Ba in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 公指命偏師，授以良圖，凌波浮湍，致屆井絡，僭豎伏鑕，梁、岷草偃。

translations.literal: Gaozu pointed and ordered a detached army; he entrusted them with a good plan; crossing waves and floating rapids, they arrived at the well rope; the usurping vertical was made to bow at the executioner's block; Liang and Min lay down like grass.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent a detached force with a sound plan. They crossed the rapids, reached the heart of the region, executed the usurper, and pacified Liang and Min.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too is Gaozu's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: This too was his achievement.

sentences.zh: 馬休、魯宗，阻兵內侮，驅率二方，連旗稱亂。

translations.literal: Ma Xiu and Lu Zong blocked the army and insulted within; they drove and led the two regions; they linked banners and called it rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xiu and Lu Zong took up arms in the interior, rallied two regions, and raised rebellion.

sentences.zh: 公投袂星言，研其上略，江津之師，勢踰風電，迴斾沔川，實繁震懾，二叛奔迸，荊、雍來蘇，玄澤浸育，溫風潛被。

translations.literal: Gaozu threw his sleeves and spoke like a star; he studied their upper strategy; the army at the river crossing—its momentum exceeded wind and lightning; turning the banners on the Mian River, the reality was abundant shock and fear; the two rebels ran and bolted; Jing and Yong came back to life; the dark beneficence soaked and nurtured; the warm wind secretly spread.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu moved like a star, outgeneraled them, and struck at the river crossing with the force of wind and lightning. The rebels fled; Jing and Yong revived under his nurturing rule.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too is Gaozu's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: This too was his achievement.

sentences.zh: 永嘉不競，四夷擅華，五都幅裂，山陵幽辱，祖宗懷沒世之憤，遺氓有匪風之思。

translations.literal: The Yongjia reign did not compete; the four barbarians usurped China; the five capitals were torn apart; mountains and tombs suffered hidden insult; the ancestors harbored the indignation of perishing in the age; the remnant people had the thought of unrighteous wind.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yongjia the barbarians had seized China; the five capitals were lost; the tombs lay in shame. The dead cried for vengeance; the living yearned for restoration.

sentences.zh: 公遠齊伊宰納隍之仁，近同小白滅亡之恥，鞠旅陳師，赫然大號，分命羣帥，北徇司、兗。

translations.literal: Gaozu from afar aligned with the benevolence of the Yi minister who received the drowning; near at hand he shared the shame of the small white who extinguished extinction; he gathered troops and arrayed the army; he blazed forth with a great proclamation; he divided commands to the crowd of marshals and marched north along Si and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu matched the Yi Yin who saved the drowning king and the Duke of Qi who avenged a fallen state. He raised his army, proclaimed a great crusade, and sent his generals north to Si and Yan.

sentences.zh: 許、鄭風靡，鞏、洛載清，偽牧逆藩，交臂請罪，百年榛穢，一朝掃滌。

translations.literal: Xu and Zheng bent to the wind; Gong and Luo were loaded with clarity; false governors and rebellious frontier lords crossed arms and requested guilt; a hundred years of thorn and filth—in one morning were swept clean.
translations.idiomatic: Xu and Zheng submitted; Gong and Luo were cleared. False governors and rebel lords surrendered. A century of ruin was swept away in a morning.

sentences.zh: [8]此又公之功也。

translations.literal: [8] This too is Gaozu's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: [8] This too was his achievement.

sentences.zh: 公有康宇內之勳，重之以明德。

translations.literal: Gaozu has the achievement of bringing peace within the four seas, heavy with bright virtue besides.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu has brought peace to the realm, and his virtue matches his deeds.

sentences.zh: 爰初發迹，則奇謨冠古，電擊強妖，則鋒無前對，聿寧東畿，大造黔首。

translations.literal: When he first set forth on the trail, then his strange plans crowned antiquity; lightning struck strong demons; his edge had none before it to face; he tranquilly settled the eastern capital region and greatly made the black-headed people.
translations.idiomatic: From his first rise his plans surpassed the ancients. He struck down mighty rebels with lightning speed, pacified the eastern capital, and saved the people.

sentences.zh: 若乃草昧經綸，化融於歲計，扶危靜亂，道固於苞桑。

translations.literal: As for grass and darkness in the warp and woof of rule, transformation melted within the year's reckoning; propping peril and quieting disorder—the Way was firm in the mulberry bud.
translations.idiomatic: In founding the state he transformed the realm year by year; in saving it from peril he made the Way firm as the mulberry root.

sentences.zh: 辯方正位，納之軌度，蠲削煩苛，較若畫一，淳風美化，盈塞宇宙。

translations.literal: He distinguished squareness and set positions, bringing them into track and measure; he abolished and cut away troublesome severity, comparing as if drawn with one stroke; pure wind and beautiful teaching filled and blocked the universe.
translations.idiomatic: He set order in the realm, cut away harsh laws with uniform fairness, and spread pure civilization throughout the world.

sentences.zh: 是以絕域獻琛，遐夷納貢，王略所宣，九服率從。

translations.literal: Therefore the cut-off domains presented treasures; distant barbarians brought tribute; where the royal plan was proclaimed, the nine services followed in accord.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the farthest lands sent tribute and all the nine regions followed his rule.

sentences.zh: 雖文命之東漸西被，咎繇之邁于種德，何以尚茲。

translations.literal: Though Yu the Great's eastward flow and westward spread, and Gao Yao's surpassing in planting virtue—how could they be placed above this?
translations.idiomatic: Not even Yu the Great's reach east and west, nor Gao Yao's virtue in planting goodness, could surpass this.

sentences.zh: 朕聞先王之宰世也，庸勳尊賢，建侯胙土，褒以寵章，崇其徽物，所以協輔皇家，永隆藩屏。

translations.literal: I have heard that when the former kings governed the world, they employed merit and honored the worthy, established marquises and enfeoffed with soil, praised them with favoring seals, and exalted their emblematic objects—thereby to assist and support the royal house and forever elevate the frontier screen.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the ancient kings governed by honoring merit and the worthy, enfeoffing lords and rewarding them with honors, so that they might support the throne and guard the realm forever.

sentences.zh: 故曲阜光啟，遂荒徐宅，營丘表海，四履有聞。

translations.literal: Therefore Qufu was brightly opened and then the wilds of Xu were extended; Yingqiu faced the sea and on four legs there was renown.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Qufu was glorified and Xu extended; Yingqiu looked to the sea and its fame reached the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 其在襄王，亦賴匡霸，又命晉文，備物光錫。

translations.literal: In the case of King Xiang, he also relied on rectifying hegemony; again he ordered Duke Wen of Jin, and complete objects were brightly bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: King Xiang too relied on hegemons to restore order; he richly rewarded Duke Wen of Jin with full honors.

sentences.zh: 惟公道冠前烈，勳高振古，而殊典未加，朕甚懵焉。

translations.literal: Only Gaozu's Way crowns former blazing deeds; his achievement is high and shakes antiquity—yet the extraordinary canon has not been added; I am very dull indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's virtue surpasses the ancients and his merit shakes history, yet the highest honors have not been granted. I am deeply at fault.

sentences.zh: 今進授相國，以徐州之彭城沛蘭陵下邳淮陽山陽廣陵、兗州之高平魯泰山十郡，封公為宋公。

translations.literal: Now I advance and confer Chief Minister, with the ten commanderies of Pengcheng, Pei, Lanling, Xiapi, Huaiyang, Shanyang, and Guangling in Xuzhou, and Gaoping, Lu, and Taishan in Yanzhou, and enfeoff Gaozu as Duke of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Now I make him Chief Minister and Duke of Song over ten commanderies: Pengcheng, Pei, Lanling, Xiapi, Huaiyang, Shanyang, and Guangling in Xu, and Gaoping, Lu, and Taishan in Yan.

sentences.zh: 錫茲玄土，苴以白茅，爰定爾居，用建冢社。

translations.literal: Bestow this dark earth, wrap it with white thatch, thereby fix your dwelling, and use it to establish the altar of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: I bestow this sacred earth wrapped in white thatch, that you may fix your dwelling and establish your altar of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 昔晉、鄭啟藩，入作卿士，周、邵保傅，出總二南，內外之重，公實兼之。

translations.literal: In former times Jin and Zheng opened the frontier and entered to serve as chief ministers; Zhou and Shao protected and tutored, going out to oversee the two souths—of inner and outer weight, Gaozu truly combines them.
translations.idiomatic: Of old Jin and Zheng were frontier lords who became chief ministers; the dukes of Zhou and Shao tutored the heir and governed abroad. Gaozu unites both roles.

sentences.zh: 今命使持節、兼太尉、尚書左僕射、晉寧縣五等男湛授相國印綬，[9]宋公璽紱；

translations.literal: Now I order the commissioner with credentials, concurrently Grand Commandant, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Baron of the Fifth Rank of Jinning County Zhan, to confer the Chief Minister's seals and cord [9] and the Duke of Song's seals and sash;
translations.idiomatic: I send Commissioner Zhan, Grand Commandant and Left Vice Director, Baron of Jinning, to confer the Chief Minister's seals and cord [9] and the Duke of Song's seals and sash.

sentences.zh: 使持節、兼司空、散騎常侍、尚書、陽遂鄉侯泰授宋公茅土，金虎符第一至第五左，[10]竹使符第一至第十左。

translations.literal: the commissioner with credentials, concurrently Minister of Works, Regular Attendant, Master of Writing, Marquis of Yangsui Township Tai, to confer on the Duke of Song the thatch earth, the golden tiger tally first through fifth on the left, [10] and the bamboo envoy tally first through tenth on the left.
translations.idiomatic: I send Commissioner Tai, Minister of Works and Master of Writing, Marquis of Yangsui, to confer the enfeoffment earth, golden tiger tallies one through five on the left [10], and bamboo envoy tallies one through ten on the left.

sentences.zh: 相國位無不總，禮絕朝班，居常之名，宜與事革。

translations.literal: The Chief Minister's position—none he does not oversee; his rites cut off the court ranks; the name used in ordinary times should change with the affair.
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Minister oversees all affairs and stands above the court. His ordinary title should change with his new office.

sentences.zh: 其以相國總百揆，[11]去「錄尚書」之號。

translations.literal: Let him as Chief Minister oversee the hundred duties [11] and remove the title "Recording the Masters of Writing."
translations.idiomatic: Let him as Chief Minister oversee all government [11] and drop the title Recording the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 上送所假節、侍中貂蟬、中外都督太傅太尉印綬，[12]豫章公印策。

translations.literal: Send up the borrowed tally, Attendant's sable cicada, seals and cord of Grand Commander of Court and Country, Grand Tutor and Grand Commandant, [12] and the Duke of Yuzhang's seal and mandate document.
translations.idiomatic: He shall return the borrowed tally, Attendant's regalia, seals of Grand Commander, Grand Tutor, and Grand Commandant [12], and the Duke of Yuzhang's seal and mandate.

sentences.zh: 進揚州牧，領征西將軍、司豫北徐雍四州刺史如故。

translations.literal: Advance him to Governor of Yangzhou, holding concurrently General Who Campaigns West and the four provinces of Si, Yu, Northern Xu, and Yong as before.
translations.idiomatic: He is advanced to Governor of Yangzhou, retaining General Who Campaigns West and the governorships of Si, Yu, Northern Xu, and Yong.

sentences.zh: 公紀綱禮度，萬國是式，乘介蹈方，罔有遷志。

translations.literal: Gaozu's warp and woof of rites and measure are the model for the ten thousand states; riding the go-between and treading the square, he has no shifting will.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's governance is the model for all states. He holds firm to the right path and never wavers.

sentences.zh: 是以錫公大輅、戎輅各一，玄牡二駟。

translations.literal: Therefore he is bestowed a great chariot and a military chariot, each one, and dark stallions in a team of four.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore he is granted a great chariot and a war chariot, each with a team of four dark stallions.

sentences.zh: 公抑末敦本，務農重積，采蘩實殷，稼穡惟阜。

translations.literal: Gaozu restrains the branch and honors the root, devotes himself to agriculture and values accumulation; he gathers duckweed and the harvest is abundant; grain crops alone are lofty.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu honors the root over the branch, devotes himself to farming, and gathers rich harvests.

sentences.zh: 是用錫公袞冕之服，赤舄副焉。

translations.literal: For this he is bestowed the robe and cap of the highest rank, with red shoes as adjunct.
translations.idiomatic: For this he is granted the highest robe and cap, with red shoes.

sentences.zh: 公閑邪納正，移風改俗，陶鈞品物，如樂之和。

translations.literal: Gaozu checks evil and receives the upright, shifts the wind and changes custom, potters and balances all things like the harmony of music.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu corrects evil and upholds the right, transforms customs, and shapes all things as music shapes harmony.

sentences.zh: 是用錫公軒縣之樂，六佾之舞。

translations.literal: For this he is bestowed the music of the elevated bells and the dance of six rows.
translations.idiomatic: For this he is granted royal music and the six-row dance.

sentences.zh: 公宣美王化，導揚休風，華夷企踵，遠人胥萃。

translations.literal: Gaozu proclaims beautiful royal transformation, guides and raises fine wind; Chinese and barbarians stand on tiptoe; distant men all gather.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu spreads royal civilization and fine customs; Chinese and barbarians alike look to him, and distant peoples gather.

sentences.zh: 是用錫公朱戶以居。

translations.literal: For this he is bestowed vermilion doors to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: For this he is granted vermilion doors for his dwelling.

sentences.zh: 公官方任能，網羅幽滯，九臯辭野，髦士盈朝。

translations.literal: Gaozu in official posts employs the able; his net gathers the hidden and stagnant; from the nine marshes they leave the wild; eminent gentlemen fill the court.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu appoints the able and gathers the neglected; worthy men fill the court.

sentences.zh: 是用錫公納陛以登。

translations.literal: For this he is bestowed the hidden steps to ascend.
translations.idiomatic: For this he is granted the hidden steps to ascend.

sentences.zh: 公當軸處中，率下以義，式遏寇讎，清除苛慝。

translations.literal: Gaozu at the axle sits in the center, leads those below by righteousness, checks and halts bandit foes, and clears away harsh evil.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu holds the center, leads by righteousness, repels enemies, and clears away harsh wrongs.

sentences.zh: 是用錫公虎賁之士三百人。

translations.literal: For this he is bestowed three hundred tiger-guard warriors.
translations.idiomatic: For this he is granted three hundred tiger guards.

sentences.zh: 公明罰恤刑，庶獄詳允，放命干紀，罔有攸縱。

translations.literal: Gaozu clarifies punishments and comforts punishments; the many prisons are detailed and true; those who throw off commands and violate discipline—none have a place to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu clarifies punishments and judges fairly; rebels and lawbreakers have nowhere to flee.

sentences.zh: 是用錫公鈇、鉞各一。

translations.literal: For this he is bestowed an axe and a battle-axe, each one.
translations.idiomatic: For this he is granted an axe and a ceremonial axe.

sentences.zh: 公龍驤鳳矯，咫尺八紘，括囊四海，折衝無外。

translations.literal: Gaozu, dragon soaring and phoenix rising, within a foot the eight cords; he bundles the four seas in a sack; repelling the foe without nothing outside.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu soars like dragon and phoenix; within a foot he commands the eight directions, holds the four seas in his grasp, and repels every foe abroad.

sentences.zh: 是用錫公彤弓一，彤矢百，盧弓十，盧矢千。

translations.literal: For this he is bestowed one red bow, one hundred red arrows, ten black bows, and one thousand black arrows.
translations.idiomatic: For this he is granted one red bow and a hundred red arrows, ten black bows and a thousand black arrows.

sentences.zh: 公溫恭孝思，致虔禋祀，忠肅之志，儀刑萬方。

translations.literal: Gaozu is warm, respectful, filial, and thoughtful; he brings sincerity to the suburban sacrifices; his loyal and solemn will is the model and law for the ten thousand regions.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu is reverent in filial piety and sincere in sacrifice; his loyal devotion is the model for all the realm.

sentences.zh: 是用錫公秬鬯一卣，圭瓚副焉。

translations.literal: For this he is bestowed one jar of black millet wine and libation vessels as adjunct.
translations.idiomatic: For this he is granted sacred wine and libation vessels.

sentences.zh: 宋國置丞相以下，一遵舊儀。

translations.literal: In the state of Song, from Chief Minister down—all follow the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the state of Song, from Chief Minister down, all offices follow the old regulations.

sentences.zh: 欽哉！

translations.literal: Reverence!
translations.idiomatic: Reverence!

sentences.zh: 其祗服往命，茂對天休，簡恤庶邦，敬敷顯德，以終我高祖之嘉命。

translations.literal: Respectfully take the going mandate, abundantly respond to Heaven's blessing, simply comfort the many states, respectfully spread bright virtue, to complete my high ancestor's fine command.
translations.idiomatic: Reverently accept this mandate, answer Heaven's blessing, care for the people, spread your bright virtue, and fulfill my high ancestor's command.

sentences.zh: 置宋國侍中、黃門侍郎、尚書左丞、郎，隨大使奉迎。

translations.literal: Set up in the state of Song Attendant, Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, and Gentlemen, who with the great envoy will welcome and escort.
translations.idiomatic: Let Song establish Attendants, Gentlemen of the Yellow Gate, the Left Assistant Director, and Gentlemen to welcome the envoy.

translations.literal: Textual annotation marker 13.
translations.idiomatic: Textual annotation marker 13.

sentences.zh: 枹罕虜乞佛熾槃遣使詣公求効力討羌，拜平西將軍、河南公。

translations.literal: The Baoheng barbarian Qifu Chipan sent an envoy to Gaozu requesting to offer strength in attacking the Qiang; he was made General Who Pacifies the West and Duke of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Chipan of Baoheng sent envoys offering to join the campaign against the Qiang. He was made General Who Pacifies the West and Duke of Henan.

sentences.zh: 十三年正月，公以舟師進討，留彭城公義隆鎮彭城。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirteenth year Gaozu advanced by water army in campaign; he left Duke of Pengcheng Yilong to garrison Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the thirteenth year Gaozu marched by river. He left Yilong, Duke of Pengcheng, to guard the city.

sentences.zh: 軍次留城，經張良廟，令曰：「夫盛德不泯，義在祀典，微管之歎，撫事彌深。

translations.literal: The army halted at Liucheng; passing Zhang Liang's temple, he ordered: "When great virtue is not extinguished, righteousness lies in the sacrificial canon; the sigh over Guan Zhong—stroking the affair, it grows deeper.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Liucheng. At Zhang Liang's temple Gaozu ordered: "Great virtue never dies and belongs in the sacrifices. The sigh over Guan Zhong grows deeper as I reflect on his deeds.

sentences.zh: 張子房道亞黃中，照隣殆庶，風雲玄感，[14]蔚為帝師，大拯橫流，夷項定漢，固以參軌伊、望，冠德如仁。

translations.literal: Zhang Zifang's Way was next to the yellow center, illuminating neighbors nearly like commoners; wind and clouds with dark resonance [14] flourished as emperor's teacher; he greatly rescued the crosscurrent, leveled Xiang and fixed Han—thus he joined the track of Yi and Wang, crowned virtue like benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liang's wisdom neared the sage's center and lit the world around him. By heaven's sign [14] he became the emperor's teacher, saved the realm from flood, overthrew Xiang Yu, and founded Han—equal to Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou in virtue.

sentences.zh: 若乃神交圯上，道契商洛，顯晦之間，窈然難究，源流淵浩，莫測其端矣。

translations.literal: As for spiritual communion on the bridge, the Way joined with Shang and Luo; between the manifest and hidden it was deep and hard to investigate; the source stream was vast and remote—none could measure its head.
translations.idiomatic: His meeting with the old man on the bridge and his pact at Shangluo lie between the seen and unseen, profound beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 塗次舊沛，佇駕留城，靈廟荒殘，遺象陳昧，撫迹懷人，慨然永歎。

translations.literal: On the road I passed old Pei and halted my chariot at Liucheng; the spirit temple was desolate and ruined, the surviving images dim and obscure; stroking the traces I cherished the man and sighed in permanence.
translations.idiomatic: Passing old Pei I halted at Liucheng. The temple lay in ruins, its images faded. I stroked the traces of his deeds and sighed.

sentences.zh: 過大梁者或佇想於夷門，遊九原者亦流連於隨會。

translations.literal: Those who passed Daliang sometimes stood longing at the Yimen; those who traveled the nine plains also lingered at Sui Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers at Daliang still pause at the Yimen Gate; travelers on the plain still linger at the grave of Zi Chan.

sentences.zh: 可改構榱桷，修飾丹青，蘋蘩行潦，以時致薦。

translations.literal: The rafters may be rebuilt, the red and green repaired; duckweed and traveling water—at the proper season offer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Let the rafters be rebuilt, the paintings restored, and offerings of duckweed and water made in season.

sentences.zh: 以紓懷古之情，用存不刊之烈。

translations.literal: To release the feeling of cherishing antiquity, and thereby preserve undying blazing deeds.
translations.idiomatic: Thus may we ease our longing for the past and preserve his undying fame.

sentences.zh: 」天子追贈公祖為太常，父為左光祿大夫，讓不受。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven posthumously enfeoffed Gaozu's grandfather as Minister of Ceremonies and his father as Left Household Master of Light; he declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor posthumously honored Gaozu's grandfather as Minister of Ceremonies and his father as Left Household Master of Light. Gaozu declined.

sentences.zh: 二月，冠軍將軍檀道濟等次潼關。

translations.literal: In the second month Champion General Tan Daoji and others halted at Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Tan Daoji and other generals reached Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 三月庚辰，大軍入河。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen in the third month the great army entered the river.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengchen in the third month the main army crossed the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 索虜步騎十萬，營據河津。

translations.literal: The northern barbarians' infantry and cavalry in the tens of thousands camped and held the river crossing.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred thousand northern barbarian horse and foot held the river crossing.

sentences.zh: 公命諸軍濟河擊破之。

translations.literal: Gaozu ordered the armies to cross the river and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu ordered his armies across the river and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 公至洛陽。

translations.literal: Gaozu reached Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu reached Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 七月，至陝城。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he reached Shancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he reached Shancheng.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍王鎮惡伐木為舟，自河浮渭。

translations.literal: Flying-Dragon General Wang Zhen'e cut wood to make boats and from the river floated onto the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen'e, Flying-Dragon General, built boats of wood and sailed from the Yellow River onto the Wei.

sentences.zh: 八月，扶風太守沈田子大破姚泓於藍田。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Fufeng Administrator Shen Tianzi greatly defeated Yao Hong at Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Shen Tianzi, Administrator of Fufeng, routed Yao Hong at Lantian.

sentences.zh: 王鎮惡剋長安，生擒泓。

translations.literal: Wang Zhen'e took Chang'an and captured Hong alive.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen'e took Chang'an and captured Hong alive.

sentences.zh: 九月，公至長安。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Gaozu reached Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Gaozu reached Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 長安豐全，帑藏盈積。

translations.literal: Chang'an was abundant and complete; the treasury stores were full and accumulated.
translations.idiomatic: Chang'an was rich and its treasuries full.

sentences.zh: 公先收其彝器、渾儀、土圭之屬，獻于京師；

translations.literal: Gaozu first collected its ritual vessels, armillary sphere, earth square, and the like, and presented them to the capital;
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu first sent its ritual vessels, armillary sphere, and earth square to the capital;

sentences.zh: 其餘珍寶珠玉，以班賜將帥。

translations.literal: the rest of the precious treasures, pearls, and jade he distributed in bestowal to the marshals and commanders.
translations.idiomatic: and distributed the rest of the jewels and treasures among his generals.

sentences.zh: 執送姚泓，斬于建康市。

translations.literal: He had Yao Hong escorted and presented; he was beheaded in the market of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong was sent to the capital and beheaded in the market at Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 謁漢高帝陵，大會文武於未央殿。

translations.literal: He visited the tomb of the High Emperor of Han and held a great assembly of civil and military men in Weiyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He visited the tomb of Emperor Gaozu of Han and held a great assembly of civil and military officials in Weiyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 十月，天子詔曰：

translations.literal: In the tenth month the Son of Heaven's edict said:
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the emperor's edict said:

sentences.zh: 朕聞先王之莅天下也，上則大寶以尊德，下則建侯以褒功。

translations.literal: I have heard that when the former kings faced the world below Heaven, above they took the great treasure to honor virtue; below they established marquises to praise achievement.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the ancient kings ruled by honoring virtue above and rewarding merit below with enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 是以成勳告就，文命有玄圭之錫，四海來王，姬旦饗龜、蒙之封。

translations.literal: Therefore when accomplished merit was announced complete, Wen the Great had the dark jade scepter bestowed; when the four seas came as kings, the Duke of Zhou enjoyed the fiefs of tortoise and Meng.
translations.idiomatic: When great deeds were done, Yu received the dark jade scepter; when the realm submitted, the Duke of Zhou received the fiefs of tortoise and Meng.

sentences.zh: 夫翼聖宣績，輔德弘猷，禮窮元賞，寵章希世。

translations.literal: To assist the sage and proclaim achievement, to support virtue and enlarge the plan—rites exhaust the highest reward; favoring seals are rare in the age.
translations.idiomatic: To assist the sage, proclaim achievement, support virtue, and enlarge the state—the highest rewards of ritual are rare in any age.

sentences.zh: 況明保沖昧，獨運陶鈞者哉！

translations.literal: How much the more for one who brightly protects tender dimness and alone turns the potter's wheel!
translations.idiomatic: How much more for one who guards a young throne and turns the potter's wheel alone!

sentences.zh: 朕以不德，遭家多難，雲雷作屯，夷羿竊命，失位京邑，遂播蠻荊，艱難卑約，制命凶醜。

translations.literal: I, lacking virtue, encountered the house with many difficulties; cloud and thunder made hardship; Yi of the east stole the mandate; I lost my place in the capital city and was driven to the southern barbarians; in hardship, lowliness, and abasement I was constrained by the mandate of vicious villains.
translations.idiomatic: I lack virtue and my house has known many troubles. Yi seized power; I lost the capital and fled to the south, living in hardship under vicious rebels.

sentences.zh: 相國宋公，天縱睿聖，命世應期，誠貫三靈，大節宏發。

translations.literal: Chief Minister of Song Liu Yu was Heaven-sent with sage wisdom, responding to the age by fate; sincerity penetrated the three spirits; great integrity blazed forth.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Liu Yu of Song is Heaven's sage, born for this age. His sincerity moves heaven; his great integrity blazes forth.

sentences.zh: 拯朕躬於巢幕，迴靈命於已崩，固已道窮北面，暉格八表者矣。

translations.literal: He rescued Our person from the nest curtain and turned the spirit mandate from already collapsed—thus his Way has exhausted facing north, and his radiance grids the eight regions.
translations.idiomatic: He saved me from ruin and restored the fallen mandate. His virtue shines on all the realm.

sentences.zh: 及外積全國之勳，內累戡黎之伐，芟夷強妖之始，蘊崇姦猾之源，顯仁藏用之道，六府孔修之績，莫不雲行雨施，能事必舉，諒已方軌於三、五，不容於典策者焉。

translations.literal: And as outwardly he accumulated achievement of completing the state, inwardly he piled achievement of conquering the black-headed people—at the beginning of cutting down and leveling strong demons, at the source where treacherous scoundrels were heaped up, the Way of displaying benevolence and concealing use, the achievement whereby the six treasuries were greatly repaired—none were not cloud moving and rain deploying; what could be done was certainly raised; truly he has squared the track of the Three and Five and cannot be contained in the canon and records.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly he completed the state; inwardly he pacified the people. He destroyed rebels at their source, restored government, and renewed the six ministries. His deeds match the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors and exceed what records can contain.

sentences.zh: 自永嘉喪師，綿踰十紀，五都分崩，然正朔時暨；

translations.literal: Since Yongjia lost its army, stretching over more than ten reigns, the five capitals were torn apart—yet the correct calendar at times still arrived;
translations.idiomatic: Since Yongjia the army was lost and for ten reigns the five capitals were torn apart, yet the calendar still held;

sentences.zh: 唯三秦懸隔，未之暫賓。

translations.literal: only the three Qin hung apart and for a time were not guests.
translations.idiomatic: only the three Qin stood apart and did not submit.

sentences.zh: 至令羌虜襲亂，淫虐三世，資百二之易守，恃函谷之可關，廟算韜略，不謀之日久矣。

translations.literal: Down to now the Qiang barbarians have inherited disorder, licentious and cruel through three generations; relying on the ease of holding the hundred-and-two, trusting that Hangu Pass could be closed—the temple calculations and hidden plans were not discussed for many days.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang have ruled in disorder for three generations, trusting in their strongholds and Hangu Pass. Long have they defied our plans.

sentences.zh: 公命世撫運，闡曜威靈，內研諸侯之慮，外致上天之罰。

translations.literal: Gaozu by fate of the age calmed the cycle, unfolded and displayed martial spirit; inwardly he studied the lords' concerns, outwardly he brought down Heaven's punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu by destiny calmed the age, displayed martial glory, read the lords' minds within, and brought Heaven's punishment without.

sentences.zh: 故能倉兕甫訓，則許、鄭風偃，鉦鉞未指，則瀍、洛霧披。

translations.literal: Therefore when the storehouse rhinoceros had just been trained, Xu and Zheng bent to the wind; before battle-axes and halberds were pointed, Chan and Luo were parted by mist.
translations.idiomatic: At the first muster Xu and Zheng submitted; before weapons were raised, Chan and Luo were cleared.

sentences.zh: 俾舊闕之陽，復集萬國之軫，東京父老，重覩司隸之章。

translations.literal: He made the yang of the old breach again gather the chariot-pins of the ten thousand states; the elders of the eastern capital again beheld the seal of the Director of the Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the old capital and gathered the realm. The elders of Luoyang saw the Director of the Capital's seal again.

sentences.zh: 俾朕負扆高拱，而保大洪烈。

translations.literal: He made me, back to the screen high and arched, preserve the great blazing enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: He let me sit at ease upon the throne and preserve the great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 是用遠鑒前典，延即羣謀，敬授殊錫，光啟疆宇。

translations.literal: Therefore I distantly reflect on the former canon, extend and take the counsel of the masses, respectfully confer the extraordinary bestowal, and brightly open the frontier realm.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I study the ancients, heed counsel, and confer extraordinary honors to open the realm.

sentences.zh: 乘馬之制，有陋舊章；

translations.literal: The system of chariots and horses has been narrow compared with the old regulations;
translations.idiomatic: The chariot honors granted before were too modest;

sentences.zh: 徽稱之美，未窮上爵。

translations.literal: the beauty of emblem and title has not exhausted the highest rank.
translations.idiomatic: the titles given did not reach the highest rank.

sentences.zh: 豈足以顯報懋功，允塞民望；

translations.literal: How could they be sufficient to display repayment of grand merit and truly fill the people's hope;
translations.idiomatic: They could not repay such merit or satisfy the people's hope,

sentences.zh: 藩輔王畿，長轡六合者乎。

translations.literal: to assist and support the royal capital region and long-rein the six harmonies?
translations.idiomatic: or honor one who guards the throne and holds the six directions in rein.

sentences.zh: 實以公每秉謙德，卑不可踰，難進之道，以寵為戚。

translations.literal: Truly Gaozu each time holds modest virtue—it cannot be surpassed in lowness; the Way hard to advance—he takes favor as sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Truly Gaozu is so humble it cannot be overcome; he treats honor as a burden.

sentences.zh: 是故降損盛制，且有後命也。

translations.literal: Therefore the grand system was lowered and reduced, and there was a later command as well.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I lowered the honors then, reserving a later command.

sentences.zh: 自茲迄今，洪勳彌劭，稜威九河，魏、趙底服，迴轅崤、潼，連城冰泮。

translations.literal: From then until now the great achievement has grown more strong; awl-edge authority on the nine rivers; Wei and Zhao reach the bottom of submission; turning the chariot at Xiao and Tong, linked cities melt like ice.
translations.idiomatic: Since then his merit has grown. He awed the nine rivers; Wei and Zhao submitted. He turned at Xiao and Tong and cities fell like melting ice.

sentences.zh: 遂長驅灞、滻，懸旍龍門，逆虜姚泓，係頸就擒。

translations.literal: Then he drove long at Ba and Chan, hung his banners at Dragon Gate; the rebellious foe Yao Hong was bound by the neck and came to capture.
translations.idiomatic: He marched to Ba and Chan and raised his banners at Dragon Gate. The rebel Yao Hong was captured by the neck.

sentences.zh: 百稔梗穢，滌於崇朝；

translations.literal: A hundred years of choked filth was washed in one lofty morning;
translations.idiomatic: A century of ruin was washed clean in a morning;

sentences.zh: 祖宗遺憤，雪於一旦。

translations.literal: the ancestors' lingering indignation was snowed in one day.
translations.idiomatic: and the ancestors' grievance was avenged in a day.

sentences.zh: 涉禹之迹，方行天下，至于海外，罔有不服。

translations.literal: He treads the traces of Yu and is about to travel the world below Heaven; reaching to beyond the sea, none do not submit.
translations.idiomatic: He follows in Yu's tracks across the world; beyond the seas, none refuse submission.

sentences.zh: 功固萬世，其寧惟永，豈金石雅頌所能讚揚，實可以告於神明，勒銘嵩、岱者已。

translations.literal: His achievement is solid for ten thousand generations—how could it be only eternal? How could metal, stone, elegant odes, and hymns be able to praise and raise it? Truly it may be told to the spirits and carved on Song and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: His achievement will last ten thousand generations. No hymn of metal and stone can praise it enough. It should be told to the spirits and carved on Mount Song and Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 朕又聞之，周道方遠，則鸑鷟鳴岐，二南播德，則麟騶呈瑞。

translations.literal: I have also heard that when the Zhou Way was just far-reaching, then the zhuoque bird sang at Qi; when the two souths spread virtue, then the lin and sou beasts appeared as omens.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that when the Zhou way extended afar, the zhuoque sang at Qi; when virtue spread in the two souths, the lin and sou appeared as omens.

sentences.zh: 自公大號初發，爰暨告成，靈祥炳煥，不可勝紀，豈伊素雉遠至，嘉禾近歸而已哉！

translations.literal: From when Gaozu's great proclamation first issued, down to the informing of completion, numinous omens blazed and shone beyond counting—how could it be only plain pheasants coming from afar and fine grain returning near?
translations.idiomatic: From his first proclamation to his victory, auspicious signs beyond count appeared—not only white pheasants from afar and fine grain near at hand.

sentences.zh: 朕每仰鑒玄應，俯察人謀，進惟道勳，退惟國典，豈得遂公沖挹，而久蘊盛策。

translations.literal: I each time look up and reflect on the dark responses, bow and examine human plans; advancing I consider the Way's achievement, retreating I consider the state's canon—how can I follow Gaozu's lofty restraint and long hoard the grand plan?
translations.idiomatic: I read heaven's signs and men's counsel, weigh merit against law, and cannot let Gaozu's humility delay the grand honor longer.

sentences.zh: 便宜敬行大禮，允副幽顯之望。

translations.literal: It is fitting to respectfully carry out the great rites and truly fulfill the hidden and manifest hopes.
translations.idiomatic: It is right to perform the supreme rites and fulfill the hope of heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 其進宋公爵為王，以徐州之海陵東安北琅邪北東莞北東海北譙北梁、豫州之汝南北潁川北南頓凡十郡，益宋國。

translations.literal: Let him advance from Duke of the state of Song to King, with the ten commanderies of Hailing, Dong'an, Northern Langye, Northern Dongguan, Northern Donghai, Northern Qiao, Northern Liang in Xuzhou, and Ruyang, Northern Yingchuan, and Northern Nandun in Yuzhou, increasing the state of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Let him advance from Duke of Song to King, adding ten commanderies: Hailing, Dong'an, Northern Langye, Northern Dongguan, Northern Donghai, Northern Qiao, and Northern Liang in Xu, and Ruyang, Northern Yingchuan, and Northern Nandun in Yu.

sentences.zh: 其相國、揚州牧、領征西將軍、司豫北徐雍四州刺史如故。

translations.literal: His Chief Minister, Governor of Yangzhou, holding General Who Campaigns West and the four provinces of Si, Yu, Northern Xu, and Yong, are as before.
translations.idiomatic: He remains Chief Minister, Governor of Yangzhou, General Who Campaigns West, and governor of Si, Yu, Northern Xu, and Yong.

sentences.zh: 十一月，前將軍劉穆之卒，以左司馬徐羨之代掌留任。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Forward General Liu Muzhi died; Left Army Marshal Xu Xianzhi was made to replace him in overseeing the duties left behind.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Liu Muzhi, Forward General, died. Xu Xianzhi, Left Army Marshal, took over the duties at headquarters.

sentences.zh: 大事昔所決於穆之者，皆悉以諮。

translations.literal: Great affairs that in former days were decided by Muzhi—all were fully consulted with him.
translations.idiomatic: All great affairs once decided by Muzhi were now referred to Xianzhi.

sentences.zh: 公欲息駕長安，經略趙、魏，會穆之卒，乃歸。

translations.literal: Gaozu wished to halt his chariot at Chang'an and plan strategy for Zhao and Wei; it happened that Muzhi died, and he then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu meant to remain at Chang'an and plan for Zhao and Wei, but Muzhi's death brought him home.

sentences.zh: 十二月庚子，發自長安，以桂陽公義真為安西將軍、雍州刺史，留腹心將佐以輔之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day gengzi, he set out from Chang'an; Duke of Guiyang Yizhen was made General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Yong, and trusted generals and assistants were left to support him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day gengzi, he left Chang'an. Yizhen, Duke of Guiyang, was made General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Yong, with trusted generals left to assist him.

sentences.zh: 閏月，公自洛入河，開汴渠以歸。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month Gaozu from Luo entered the river and opened the Bian canal to return.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month he entered the Yellow River from Luoyang and opened the Bian canal for the homeward march.

sentences.zh: 十四年正月壬戌，公至彭城，解嚴息甲。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourteenth year, on the day renxu, Gaozu reached Pengcheng, lifted martial readiness, and rested the armor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourteenth year, on the day renxu, he reached Pengcheng and stood the army down.

sentences.zh: 以輔國將軍劉遵考為并州刺史，領河東太守，鎮蒲坂。

translations.literal: Assistant General Who Assists the State Liu Zunkao was made Governor of Bing and concurrently Governor of Hedong, garrisoning Puban.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zunkao, Assistant General Who Assists the State, was made Governor of Bing and Hedong and garrisoned Puban.

sentences.zh: 公解司州，領徐、冀二州刺史，固讓進爵。

translations.literal: Gaozu relinquished Si province and took Xu and Ji; he firmly declined advancement in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu gave up Si province and took Xu and Ji, but again refused advancement in rank.

sentences.zh: 六月，受相國宋公九錫之命。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he received the mandate of Chief Minister Duke of Song and the nine bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he received the mandate of Chief Minister, Duke of Song, and the Nine Bestowals.

sentences.zh: 令曰：「孤以寡薄，負荷殊重，守位奉藩，危溢是懼。

translations.literal: He ordered: "I, solitary and thin, bear a special weight; guarding my position and serving the frontier, overflow of peril is what I fear.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered: "I am unworthy of the burden laid upon me. I guard my post and serve the throne, and fear I may fail.

sentences.zh: 朝恩隆泰，委美推功，遂方軌齊、晉，擬議國典。

translations.literal: The court's grace is lofty and abundant; entrusting beauty and pushing achievement to me, I then squared the track of Qi and Jin and was compared with the state's canon.
translations.idiomatic: The court has heaped honors on me and pushed merit my way until I stand beside Qi and Jin in the state's canon.

sentences.zh: 雖亮誠守分，十稔于今，而成命弗迴，百辟胥暨內外庶僚，敦勉周至。

translations.literal: Though I have brightly held sincerity and guarded my portion for ten years until now, the completed mandate does not turn back; the hundred officials all arrive together, inner and outer civil servants alike urging with doubled zeal to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Though I have declined for ten years, the mandate will not be refused. Officials within and without urge me on.

sentences.zh: 籍運來之功，參休明之迹，乘菲薄之資，同盛德之事，監寐永言，未知攸託。

translations.literal: Relying on the achievement that fortune brought, sharing in the traces of bright governance, riding thin and slight resources, sharing in affairs of flourishing virtue—I watch and sleep, speaking forever, not knowing what to entrust myself to.
translations.idiomatic: By fortune's gift I share in bright rule, though my means are slight. I lie awake, not knowing where this path leads.

sentences.zh: 隆祚之始，思覃斯慶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the lofty fortune I think to extend this celebration.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of this glorious age I wish to share the celebration.

sentences.zh: 其赦國內殊死以下，今月二十三日昧爽以前，悉皆原宥。

translations.literal: Let those within the state guilty of special death and below, before dawn on the twenty-third of this month, all be pardoned and released.
translations.idiomatic: Let all within the state guilty of capital crimes and below be pardoned before dawn on the twenty-third of this month.

sentences.zh: 鰥寡孤獨不能自存者，人賜粟五斛。

translations.literal: Widowers, widows, orphans, and the solitary who cannot support themselves—each person is bestowed five hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Widows, orphans, and the destitute who cannot support themselves shall receive five hu of grain each.

sentences.zh: 府州刑罪，亦同蕩然。

translations.literal: Crimes of the headquarters and provinces are likewise entirely cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Crimes in the headquarters and provinces are likewise remitted.

sentences.zh: 其餘詳依舊準。

translations.literal: The rest in detail follow the old standard."
translations.idiomatic: The rest follow the old regulations."

sentences.zh: 」詔崇豫章公太夫人為宋公太妃，世子中軍將軍，副貳相國府。

translations.literal: An edict honored the Grand Matron of Duke of Yuzhang as Grand Consort of the Duke of Song; the heir as Central Army General, deputy of the Chief Minister's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made the Grand Matron of Duke of Yuzhang Grand Consort of the Duke of Song, and the heir Central Army General, deputy at the Chief Minister's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 以太尉軍諮祭酒孔季恭為宋國尚書令，青州刺史檀祗為領軍將軍，相國左長史王弘為尚書僕射。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Army Adviser and Sacrificial Officer Kong Jigong was made Chief of the Masters of Writing of the state of Song; Governor of Qingzhou Tan Zhi as General of the Guard; Chief of Staff of the Left Wang Hong as Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Jigong was made Chief of the Masters of Writing of Song; Tan Zhi, Governor of Qingzhou, General of the Guard; and Wang Hong, Left Chief of Staff, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 其餘百官悉依天朝之制。

translations.literal: The rest of the hundred offices all followed the heavenly court's system.
translations.idiomatic: All other offices followed the imperial court's system.

sentences.zh: 又詔宋國所封十郡之外，悉得除用。

translations.literal: Again it was ordered that beyond the ten commanderies enfeoffed to the state of Song, all might be appointed and employed.
translations.idiomatic: It was also ordered that appointments might be made beyond the ten commanderies of Song.

sentences.zh: 先是安西中兵參軍沈田子殺安西司馬王鎮惡，諸將軍復殺安西長史王脩。

translations.literal: Earlier Pacifying-the-West Central Army Adviser Shen Tianzi killed Pacifying-the-West Marshal Wang Zhen'e; the generals again killed Pacifying-the-West Chief of Staff Wang Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Shen Tianzi, staff officer of the Pacifying West army, killed Wang Zhen'e, its marshal; the generals then killed Wang Xiu, its chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 關中亂。

translations.literal: Guanzhong was in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong fell into chaos.

sentences.zh: 十月，公遣右將軍朱齡石代安西將軍桂陽公義真為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Gaozu sent Right General Zhu Lingshi to replace Pacifying-the-West General Duke of Guiyang Yizhen as Governor of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Gaozu sent Zhu Lingshi, Right General, to replace Yizhen as Governor of Yong.

sentences.zh: 義真既還，為佛佛虜所追，大敗，僅以身免。

translations.literal: When Yizhen had returned, he was pursued by the Fofo barbarians, greatly defeated, and barely escaped with his person.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Yizhen was pursued by the Fofo barbarians, routed, and barely escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 諸將帥及齡石並沒。

translations.literal: The generals and commanders and Lingshi were all lost.
translations.idiomatic: The generals and Lingshi were all lost.

sentences.zh: 領軍檀祗卒，以中軍司馬檀道濟為中領軍。

translations.literal: General of the Guard Tan Zhi died; Central Army Marshal Tan Daoji was made Central General of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Zhi, General of the Guard, died. Tan Daoji, Central Army Marshal, became Central General of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 十二月，天子崩，大司馬琅邪王即帝位。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the Son of Heaven died; the Grand Marshal, Prince of Langye, took the imperial position.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the emperor died. The Grand Marshal, Prince of Langye, took the throne.

sentences.zh: 十二月，天子命王冕十有二旒，建天子旌旗，出警入蹕，乘金根車，駕六馬，備五時副車，置旄頭雲罕，樂舞八佾，設鍾虡宮縣。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the Son of Heaven ordered the king's cap with twelve tassels, established the Son of Heaven's banners and flags, going out with police and entering with imperial escort, riding the golden-root chariot, driving six horses, provided with five-season secondary chariots, setting yak-tail and cloud pennants, music and dance of eight rows, and setting bells and suspended stones in palace arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the emperor granted him the twelve-tassel cap, the Son of Heaven's banners, imperial escort, the golden-root chariot with six horses, five seasonal chariots, yak-tail and cloud pennants, eight-row dance, and palace bells.

sentences.zh: 進王太妃為太后，王妃為王后，世子為太子，王子、王孫爵命之號，一如舊儀。

translations.literal: The king's grand consort was advanced to Empress Dowager; the king's consort to Queen; the heir to Crown Prince; the titles of prince and king's grandson—all like the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was made Empress Dowager, his wife Queen, his heir Crown Prince; titles for princes and grandsons followed the old regulations.

sentences.zh: 二年四月，徵王入輔。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year the king was summoned to assist at court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year the king was summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 六月，至京師。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 晉帝禪位于王，詔曰：

translations.literal: The Jin emperor abdicated the throne to the king; the edict said:
translations.idiomatic: The Jin emperor abdicated to the king. The edict said:

sentences.zh: 夫天造草昧，樹之司牧，所以陶鈞三極，統天施化。

translations.literal: Heaven made the grass and darkness and set up ministers to herd it, thereby to potter the three poles and align Heaven in spreading transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven in the beginning made the world and set rulers over it, to harmonize the three realms and carry out Heaven's transforming work.

sentences.zh: 故大道之行，選賢與能，隆替無常期，禪代非一族，貫之百王，由來尚矣。

translations.literal: Therefore when the great Way proceeds, the worthy are selected and the able employed; rise and fall have no constant term; abdication and succession are not of one clan—threading through the hundred kings, from of old it has been honored.
translations.idiomatic: When the great Way prevails, the worthy rule. Dynasties rise and fall without fixed term; abdication passes power beyond one clan. This has been honored through all kings.

sentences.zh: 晉道陵遲，仍世多故，爰暨元興，禍難既積，至三光貿位，冠履易所，安皇播越，宗祀墮泯，則我宣、元之祚，永墜于地，顧瞻區域，翦焉已傾。

translations.literal: The Jin Way declined and lagged; generation after generation had many troubles; reaching Yuanxing, calamity and hardship had accumulated; down to the three luminaries trading places, crown and shoes changed their station; Emperor An was driven about, the ancestral sacrifices toppled and extinguished—then the fortune of Xuan and Yuan forever fell to the ground; looking back on the realm, it was already cut down and toppled.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin dynasty declined through age after age of trouble. The throne was overturned, Emperor An was driven into exile, and the ancestral rites perished. The fortunes of Xuan and Yuan fell to earth; the realm lay in ruins.

sentences.zh: 相國宋王，天縱聖德，靈武秀世，一匡頹運，再造區夏，固以興滅繼絕，舟航淪溺矣。

translations.literal: Chief Minister of Song was Heaven-sent with sage virtue; spiritual martiality flourished in the age; once he rectified the declining cycle and remade the realm within the four quarters—thus he continued the dying and restored the cut off, a boat and raft for those drowned in the flood.
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Minister of Song is Heaven's sage, whose martial spirit renews the age. He restored the fallen dynasty and saved the drowning realm.

sentences.zh: 若夫仰在璿璣，旁穆七政，薄伐不庭，開復疆宇。

translations.literal: As for looking up to the jade pivots and beside them harmonizing the seven regulators, making light campaign against those not at court, opening and recovering frontier territory—
translations.idiomatic: He aligned the heavens, pacified the borders, and opened the frontiers—

sentences.zh: 遂乃三俘偽主，開滌五都，雕顏卉服之鄉，龍荒朔漠之長，莫不迴首朝陽，沐浴玄澤。

translations.literal: then he three times captured false rulers, opened and washed the five capitals; in villages of tattooed faces and flowery dress, and among chiefs of the dragon wilds and northern deserts—none did not turn their heads to the morning sun and bathe in the dark beneficence.
translations.idiomatic: he captured three false rulers, restored the five capitals, and brought tattooed barbarians and desert chiefs to turn toward the court and bathe in his grace.

sentences.zh: 故四靈効瑞，川岳啟圖，嘉祥雜遝，休應炳著，玄象表革命之期，華裔注樂推之願。

translations.literal: Therefore the four numina effected auspicious omens; rivers and mountains opened their charts; fine omens were mixed and abundant; fine responses blazed and showed; the dark images displayed the term of revolution; Chinese and barbarians poured forth the wish to push him forward.
translations.idiomatic: The four spirits sent omens; rivers and mountains revealed signs. Heaven showed the term of revolution; Chinese and barbarians alike wished to enthrone him.

sentences.zh: 代德之符，著乎幽顯，瞻烏爰止，允集明哲，夫豈延康有歸，咸熙告謝而已哉！

translations.literal: The talisman of changing virtue was fixed in the hidden and manifest; gazing at the crow they stop—truly the wise gather. How could it be only that Yankang had its return and Xianxi announced farewell!
translations.idiomatic: The mandate to change virtue was clear to heaven and earth. The wise all gather to him. This is more than the passing of Yankang or the farewell of Xianxi.

sentences.zh: 昔火德既微，魏祖底績，黃運不競，三后肆勤。

translations.literal: In former days the fire virtue was already slight; the Wei ancestor settled the achievement; the yellow cycle did not compete; the three queens ran riot in toil.
translations.idiomatic: When fire virtue waned, Wei received the mandate; when the yellow cycle failed, the three queens toiled in turn.

sentences.zh: 故天之曆數，實有攸在。

translations.literal: Therefore Heaven's calendar and number truly have what they rest in.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's calendar truly has its appointed lord.

sentences.zh: 朕雖庸闇，昧於大道，永鑒廢興，為日已久。

translations.literal: I, though mediocre and dim, am dull in the great Way; forever reflecting on abolition and rise—for many days it has been long.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am dull and weak in the great Way, I have long watched rise and fall.

sentences.zh: 念四代之高義，稽天人之至望，予其遜位別宮，歸禪于宋，一依唐虞、漢魏故事。

translations.literal: Thinking on the high righteousness of the four ages, examining the utmost hope of Heaven and men—I will yield the position to a separate palace and abdicate to Song, all following the stories of Tang-Yu and Han-Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering the righteousness of the four ages and the hope of Heaven and men, I yield the throne to Song, following the precedents of Tang-Yu and Han-Wei.

sentences.zh: 詔草既成，送呈天子使書之，天子即便操筆，謂左右曰：「桓玄之時，天命已改，重為劉公所延，將二十載。

translations.literal: When the draft edict was complete it was sent and presented to the Son of Heaven to have him write it; the Son of Heaven then at once took up the brush and said to those at his side: "In the time of Huan Xuan Heaven's mandate had already changed; I was again extended by Duke Liu for nearly twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: When the abdication edict was drafted, it was sent to the emperor to copy. He took the brush at once and said to those beside him: "Under Huan Xuan the mandate had already changed. Duke Liu extended my reign for nearly twenty years.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，本所甘心。

translations.literal: Today's affair is originally what my heart is willing for."
translations.idiomatic: Today's affair is what my heart has long accepted."

sentences.zh: 」甲子，策曰：

translations.literal: On the day jiazi the mandate document said:
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiazi the mandate read:

sentences.zh: 咨爾宋王：夫玄古權輿，悠哉邈矣，其詳靡得而聞。

translations.literal: Consult you, King of Song: the dark antiquity when power first arose—how far and remote! Its details cannot be heard.
translations.idiomatic: To you, King of Song: in deepest antiquity, when rule first arose, the details are lost in time.

sentences.zh: 爰自書契，降逮三、五，莫不以上聖君四海，止戈定大業。

translations.literal: From when writing and tallies descended down to the Three and Five, none did not use the highest sage to lord the four seas, stop weapons and fix the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: From the age of writing down to the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, sages ruled the four seas, stopped war, and fixed the great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 然則帝王者，宰物之通器；

translations.literal: Thus the emperor and king is the common vessel for ruling things;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor is the vessel for ruling all things;

sentences.zh: 君道者，天下之至公。

translations.literal: the Way of the ruler is the utmost fairness under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: the ruler's way is the utmost fairness under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 昔在上葉，深鑒茲道，是以天祿既終，唐、虞弗得傳其嗣；

translations.literal: In former days in the upper age, deeply reflecting on this Way, therefore when Heaven's blessing had ended, Tang and Yu could not transmit their heirs;
translations.idiomatic: In high antiquity, when Heaven's blessing ended, Tang and Yu could not pass the throne to their sons;

sentences.zh: 符命來格，舜、禹不獲全其謙。

translations.literal: when the mandate's talisman came, Shun and Yu could not preserve their modesty whole.
translations.idiomatic: when the mandate came, Shun and Yu could not keep their modest refusal.

sentences.zh: 所以經緯三才，澄序彝化，作範振古，垂風萬葉，莫尚於茲。

translations.literal: Therefore to weave the three powers, clarify and order the transforming norms, make a model to shake antiquity, and hand down wind for ten thousand generations—nothing is greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they ordered the three realms, set the transforming norms, made models for all time, and handed down virtue for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 自是厥後，歷代彌劭，漢既嗣德於放勛，魏亦方軌於重華。

translations.literal: From this thereafter, generation after generation grew more emphatic; Han continued the virtue of Emperor Yao; Wei also squared the track of Chonghua.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter each age grew stronger in this: Han followed Yao's virtue; Wei matched Shun's track.

sentences.zh: 諒以協謀乎人鬼，而以百姓為心者也。

translations.literal: Truly they coordinated plans between men and ghosts, and took the hundred surnames as heart.
translations.idiomatic: They harmonized men and spirits and took the people as their heart.

sentences.zh: 昔我祖宗欽明，辰居其極，而明晦代序，盈虧有期。

translations.literal: In former days our ancestors were reverent and bright; The Star dwelt at the pole; yet bright and dark succeeded in order; fullness and deficit had their terms.
translations.idiomatic: Our ancestors were reverent and bright, and the pole star stood firm; yet light and dark alternate, and fullness and waning have their terms.

sentences.zh: 翦商兆禍，非唯一世，曾是弗剋，矧伊在今，天之所廢，有自來矣。

translations.literal: The omen of cutting Shang brought calamity—not for one age alone; once this could not be overcome—how much more in the present! What Heaven abolishes has come from of old.
translations.idiomatic: The fall of Shang foretold calamity for many ages. Once it could not be overcome; how much less today. What Heaven abolishes has long been foretold.

sentences.zh: 惟王體上聖之姿，苞二儀之德，明齊日月，道合四時。

translations.literal: Only the king's person holds the posture of the highest sage, embraces the virtue of the two regulators, brightness equal to sun and moon, Way matching the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Only you hold the sage's stature, embrace heaven and earth's virtue, shine like sun and moon, and match the four seasons in your Way.

sentences.zh: 乃者社稷傾覆，王拯而存之，中原蕪梗，又濟而復之。

translations.literal: Then the altars of state toppled and overturned—the king rescued and preserved them; the central plains were wasteland and blocked—again he crossed and restored them.
translations.idiomatic: When the altars fell, you saved them; when the central plains lay waste, you restored them.

sentences.zh: 自負固不賓，干紀放命，肆逆滔天，竊據萬里。

translations.literal: From those who relied on solidity and would not guest, to those who violated discipline and threw off mandate, running riot and flooding Heaven, stealing and occupying ten thousand li—
translations.idiomatic: From stubborn rebels to those who defied the law and seized vast territories—

sentences.zh: 靡不潤之以風雨，震之以雷霆。

translations.literal: none were not moistened with wind and rain, shaken with thunder and lightning.
translations.idiomatic: none escaped your rain of grace or thunder of wrath.

sentences.zh: 九伐之道既敷，八法之化自理。

translations.literal: The Way of the nine campaigns was already spread; the transformation of the eight methods was naturally ordered.
translations.idiomatic: The nine campaigns were carried out; the eight methods brought order.

sentences.zh: 豈伊博施於民，濟斯黔庶；

translations.literal: How could it be only spreading broadly among the people and crossing this black-headed multitude;
translations.idiomatic: You have not only enriched the people and saved the masses;

sentences.zh: 固以義洽四海，道威八荒者矣。

translations.literal: firmly righteousness has harmonized the four seas; the Way's awl-edge authority fills the eight regions.
translations.idiomatic: your righteousness fills the four seas and your authority the eight directions.

sentences.zh: 至於上天垂象，四靈效徵，圖讖之文既明，人神之望已改。

translations.literal: As for Heaven above hanging images, the four numina effecting omens, the texts of charts and prophecies already clarified, the hope of men and spirits already changed—
translations.idiomatic: Heaven shows signs; the four spirits send omens; prophecies are clear; men and spirits have turned their hope—

sentences.zh: 百工歌於朝，庶民頌于野，億兆抃踊，傾佇惟新。

translations.literal: the hundred craftsmen sing in the court; the many people chant in the wild; the hundred millions stamp and leap; leaning and waiting, they look only for the new.
translations.idiomatic: craftsmen sing in court, people chant in the fields, and all the realm leaps, awaiting the new age.

sentences.zh: 自非百姓樂推，天命攸集，豈伊在予，所得獨專。

translations.literal: Unless the hundred surnames joyfully pushed and Heaven's mandate thereby gathered—how could it be in me alone that what was obtained was exclusively held?
translations.idiomatic: Unless the people pushed and Heaven's mandate gathered, how could I hold this alone?

sentences.zh: 是用仰祗皇靈，俯順羣議，敬禪神器，授帝位于爾躬。

translations.literal: Therefore I respectfully look up to the imperial numen and bow to follow the counsel of the masses, respectfully abdicating the divine vessel and conferring the emperor's position on your person.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I reverently follow Heaven and the people's will, abdicate the throne, and confer the imperial seat upon you.

sentences.zh: 大祚告窮，天祿永終。

translations.literal: The great fortune is announced exhausted; Heaven's blessing forever ends.
translations.idiomatic: The great fortune is ended; Heaven's blessing passes away.

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 王其允執其中，敬遵典訓，副率土之嘉願，恢洪業於無窮，時膺休祐，以答三靈之眷望。

translations.literal: King, you must truly hold the center, respectfully follow the canon and instructions, assist the excellent wish of all within the lands, restore the great enterprise without end, timely receive fine blessing, to answer the three spirits' look of attachment.
translations.idiomatic: King, hold the center, follow the canon, fulfill the realm's wish, extend the great enterprise without end, receive Heaven's blessing, and answer the three spirits' regard.

sentences.zh: 又璽書曰：

translations.literal: Again the imperial letter said:
translations.idiomatic: The imperial letter also said:

sentences.zh: 蓋聞天生蒸民，樹之以君，帝皇寄世，實公四海，崇替係於勳德，升降存乎其人。

translations.literal: I have heard that Heaven gives birth to the growing people and sets up a lord for them; emperors and kings lodge in the age and truly lord the four seas; rise and fall depend on merit and virtue; advancement and decline rest in the man.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Heaven creates the people and sets a lord over them; emperors rule the four seas; rise and fall depend on merit; advancement rests in the man.

sentences.zh: 故有國必亡，卜年著其數，代謝無常，聖哲握其符。

translations.literal: Therefore having a state must perish; divining the years shows its number; generation and succession have no constancy; the sage grasps its talisman.
translations.idiomatic: States must perish; their years are numbered; dynasties change; the sage grasps the mandate.

sentences.zh: 昔在上世，三聖係軌，疇咨四嶽，以弘揖讓。

translations.literal: In former days in the upper age the three sages continued the track; they consulted the four peaks to enlarge yielding and abdication.
